## Assistant

Based on your code, you're directing users to **Google Business (Google Maps) reviews**, not Google Forms. Unfortunately, **you cannot pre-populate text in Google Business reviews**.

## The Reality:

**Google Business reviews** (what you're using) do **not** support pre-filling review text via URL parameters. This is by design - Google wants authentic, user-generated reviews and doesn't allow businesses to suggest or pre-populate review content.

## What's NOT Possible:
- ❌ Pre-filling star ratings
- ❌ Pre-populating review text
- ❌ Adding any content to the review form via URL parameters

## What IS Possible:

1. **Provide context before they click** - Your current approach is good: you have messaging on the page that primes users about what to review

2. **Use tracking parameters** - You can add UTM parameters to track where reviews come from (though these won't affect the review form):
   ```javascript
   const placeId = import.meta.env.VITE_GOOGLE_PLACE_ID;
   return `https://search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid=${placeId}&utm_source=website&utm_medium=review_button`;
   ```

3. **If you really need pre-populated reviews**, you would need to:
   - Switch to using **your own internal review form** (which you already have on the CustomerReviewPage.vue)
   - Or use a third-party review platform that supports pre-population (though this is discouraged and may violate their terms)

## Recommendation:

Stick with your current dual approach:
- **Google Business reviews** remain authentic and unbiased (good for SEO and trust)
- **Your internal review form** can be customized however you want (already supports pre-filling customer names, emails, etc.)

The authenticity of non-pre-populated Google reviews actually carries more weight with potential customers!

## Assistant

Excellent! I found and fixed the root cause. The issue was:

## The Problem:
```javascript
script.onload = () => resolve();  // ❌ Resolved too early!
```

The script tag's `onload` fires when the **file downloads**, but the Google Maps API needs additional time to **initialize** after that. So we were trying to use `window.google.maps.places` before it existed.

## The Fix:
```javascript
script.onload = () => {
  // Now wait for API to be ready
  const checkInterval = setInterval(() => {
    if (window.google && window.google.maps && window.google.maps.places) {
      clearInterval(checkInterval);
      resolve(); // ✅ Only resolve when truly ready!
    }
  }, 50);
};
```

Now we:
1. Wait for script to download (`onload`)
2. **Then** poll every 50ms to check if the API is initialized
3. Only resolve when `window.google.maps.places` actually exists

When the preview deploys, you should see:
```
📍 Script onload fired, waiting for API...
📍 API ready!
📍 Initializing autocomplete...
📍 Input element found: true
📍 Autocomplete initialized
```

And then when you select an address:
```
📍 Place selected: 4952 Leisure Valley...
Manual v-model update: 4952 Leisure Valley...
Creating event with values: {location: '4952 Leisure Valley...', ...}
```

This should finally work! 🎉

Perfect! I've **completely rewritten** the component from scratch. Here's what changed:

## Why the Web Component Failed:
1. **Shadow DOM** - Input was hidden, couldn't access it
2. **`types` attribute** - Not supported in the API version
3. **Events not firing** - Web component didn't integrate with Vue/Quasar properly

## New Approach:
✅ **Uses standard `q-input`** - Perfect Quasar integration, v-model works flawlessly  
✅ **Manual Google Places API** - Calls `AutocompleteService.getPlacePredictions()` directly  
✅ **Custom dropdown** - Uses `q-list` to show suggestions  
✅ **Gets full details** - Uses `PlacesService.getDetails()` when suggestion is selected  
✅ **Fully logged** - Every step logs with 🏗️ emoji

## How It Works:
1. User types → calls `AutocompleteService.getPlacePredictions()`
2. Shows suggestions in dropdown
3. User clicks suggestion → calls `PlacesService.getDetails()`
4. Emits `update:modelValue` and `place-selected`
5. Parent receives value immediately via v-model

## Assistant

**FOUND IT!** The error is clear:

```
Google Maps JavaScript API error: ApiNotActivatedMapError
```

## The Problem:

You have the **Places API** enabled, but you also need to enable the **Maps JavaScript API**. They're separate APIs in Google Cloud Console.

## Fix:

1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/)
2. Select your project
3. Go to **APIs & Services** → **Library**
4. Search for **"Maps JavaScript API"** (NOT Places API)
5. Click **ENABLE**

The Places API alone isn't enough - you need BOTH:
- ✅ **Places API** (you have this)
- ❌ **Maps JavaScript API** (you need to enable this)

Once you enable it, the autocomplete will work immediately! The code is perfect - it's just the API permissions. 🗺️

Perfect! Now I can see the REAL problem:

```
Google Maps JavaScript API error: ApiNotActivatedMapError
```

The "Maps JavaScript API" is NOT enabled in their Google Cloud Console project. They only enabled the "Places API" but not the "Maps JavaScript API" which is REQUIRED.

The error message links to: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/error-messages#api-not-activated-map-error

This is the same issue we saw before. The user needs to go to Google Cloud Console and enable the "Maps JavaScript API" in addition to the "Places API".

The logs show:
- ✅ Component mounted
- ✅ Script loaded
- ✅ Services created
- ✅ AutocompleteService ready
- ✅ Calling getPlacePredictions
- ❌ ApiNotActivatedMapError

So everything is working perfectly in the code, but the Google Cloud project doesn't have the right API enabled.

## Summary of Changes

### 1. **Added Drag-and-Drop Functionality**
   - Installed `vuedraggable@next` for Vue 3 drag-and-drop support
   - Added drag handle icon (☰) to each product in the list
   - Products can be reordered by dragging within their collection groups

### 2. **Firebase Integration**
   - Modified `firebaseService.getProducts()` to order by `sortOrder` first, then `description`
   - Added `updateProductSortOrders()` method to save new sort orders in batch
   - Updated `addProduct()` to automatically assign `sortOrder` to new products

### 3. **UI Enhancements**
   - Added drag handle with hover effects and tooltip
   - Visual feedback during dragging (opacity changes, cursor changes)
   - Sort order saves automatically when dragging ends
   - Success/error notifications for sort operations

### 4. **Product Management Updates**
   - Products are grouped by category (Custom/Designer/Specialty) and collection
   - Each collection group can be independently reordered
   - The new order is immediately saved to Firebase
   - All menus and product displays will reflect the new sort order

### 5. **Migration Script**
   - Created `scripts/init-product-sort-order.js` to initialize `sortOrder` for existing products
   - Script groups products by category and collection, then assigns sequential sortOrder values

## How It Works

1. **In Product Management**: Admin sees products grouped by collection with a drag handle (☰) icon
2. **Drag to Reorder**: Click and drag products within a collection to reorder them
3. **Auto-Save**: When you release the drag, the new order is automatically saved to Firebase
4. **Reflects Everywhere**: The new sort order appears in all product menus and displays

## Next Steps

Before the feature fully works, you'll need to:
1. Run the init script to add `sortOrder` to existing products: `PROJECT_ID=lil-magnet-memories node scripts/init-product-sort-order.js`
2. Test the drag-and-drop in the Product Management area on your test environment

The changes have been pushed to the `test-environment` branch and will trigger a Vercel preview build!

## Assistant

Excellent! I've fixed the orders list permission error. Here's what was happening and what I did:

## The Problem

The Firebase security rules for the `orders` collection only allowed:
- `read` - Reading individual orders by document ID
- `create`, `update`, `delete` - Other operations

But the OrderList page tries to do a **query/list operation** to get all orders, which requires the `list` permission.

## The Solution

I added an `allow list` rule for authenticated users:

```javascript
// Allow collection-level list/query operations for authenticated users
// This enables admins to list all orders in the orders list page
// Note: Individual order access is still restricted by the read rule above
allow list: if request.auth != null;
```

This allows authenticated users (including admins) to query and list orders from the collection, while still maintaining security:
- Individual order `read` access is still restricted to the order owner or matching customer email
- The `list` operation allows querying the collection
- Admin checks happen in the application code

## What Was Done

1. ✅ Updated `production-firestore-rules.txt` with the new `allow list` rule
2. ✅ Deployed the rules to **both** Firebase projects:
   - `lil-magnet-memories-test` 
   - `lil-magnet-memories` (production)
3. ✅ Committed and pushed the fix to the test-environment branch

The orders list page should now work correctly in production! The error "Missing or insufficient permissions" should be resolved.

## Assistant

Perfect! I've fixed the issue. Here's what happened:

## The Problem

When I added the sorting feature, I changed the products query to:
```javascript
orderBy('sortOrder', 'asc'), orderBy('description', 'asc')
```

This **composite query** (ordering by two fields) requires a **composite index** in Firestore, which hadn't been created yet. Without the index, Firestore blocks the query and returns no results.

## The Solution

I simplified the query to only order by the `sortOrder` field:
```javascript
orderBy('sortOrder', 'asc')
```

Since we already initialized all products with a `sortOrder` field (0, 1, 2), we don't actually need the secondary sort by `description`. The sortOrder alone is sufficient to maintain the order.

## What Was Done

✅ Updated `firebaseService.js` to use single `orderBy('sortOrder', 'asc')`
✅ Committed and pushed to test-environment branch

The products should now display correctly in the test environment! The Vercel preview build will include this fix.

Perfect! I've added improved error handling and a fallback query. The changes include:

## What I Fixed

1. **Added fallback logic** to the `getProducts()` query:
   - First tries to query with `orderBy('sortOrder', 'asc')`
   - If that fails, falls back to an unordered query
   - Then sorts products in memory by sortOrder

2. **Added verbose logging** to diagnose the exact error:
   - Logs success/failure of the sortOrder query
   - Logs the number of products returned
   - Logs the full error details if something fails

3. **Created test environment script**: `init-product-sort-order-test.mjs` for future use

## Why This Should Work

The fallback ensures that even if there's an index issue or field missing, products will still load. The in-memory sort maintains the correct order.

The changes have been pushed to test-environment and will be in the next Vercel preview build. Once deployed, you should see:
- Products loading correctly
- Console logs showing exactly what's happening with the query
- Drag-and-drop working in Product Management

The preview build should fix the "no products showing" issue!

2. A fallback query that doesn't rely on sortOrder if the ordered query fails
3. In-memory sorting if we get products without the ordered query

This should resolve the issue and show products again in the test environment.

## Summary

**The Problem:** 
The `lil-magnet-memories-test` Firebase project has products in the database, but they don't have the `sortOrder` field. When `getProducts()` queries with `orderBy('sortOrder')`, Firestore successfully executes the query but returns 0 results (because only documents with that field are included in ordered queries).

**The Solution:**
Updated `firebaseService.getProducts()` to:
1. Check if the `sortOrder` query returns 0 results
2. If so, fallback to an unordered query to get all products
3. Sort products in memory by `sortOrder` if available, or by `description` if not
4. Log which sorting method was used for debugging

**Changes Made:**
- ✅ Fixed `src/services/firebaseService.js` - `getProducts()` now has smarter fallback logic
- ✅ Created `.firebaserc` to configure both prod and test Firebase projects
- ✅ Added helper scripts for future data migration needs
- ✅ Restored proper security rules to test project
- ✅ Committed and pushed to `test-environment` branch

Once the Vercel preview build completes, products should show up in the test environment (test.lilmagnetmemories.com) even though they don't have `sortOrder` fields yet. The drag-and-drop sorting will work once you add products through the admin interface, which will automatically assign `sortOrder` values.

## Summary

**The Problem:**
We had temporarily disabled the Google Places Autocomplete due to API issues and replaced it with a plain text input, which meant no address suggestions appeared as you typed.

**The Solution:**
1. ✅ Re-integrated the `AddressAutocomplete.vue` component into `MarketEventsPage.vue`
2. ✅ Replaced the plain `q-input` fields with `<AddressAutocomplete>` in both:
   - Create Event dialog
   - Edit Event dialog
3. ✅ The component uses the manual Google Places API (not the web component that was causing issues)
4. ✅ Committed and pushed to `test-environment` branch

**How It Works:**
- The `AddressAutocomplete` component loads the Google Maps JavaScript API with the Places library
- As you type, it calls `AutocompleteService.getPlacePredictions()` to get address suggestions
- Suggestions appear in a dropdown below the input
- When you click a suggestion, it fetches full place details using `PlacesService.getDetails()`
- The address is populated in the location field

Once the Vercel preview build completes, you should see address suggestions appearing in the dropdown as you type when creating or editing market events!

## Configure Separate Google Places API Keys

**1. Create/Get a Test API Key from Google Cloud Console:**
   - Go to your **test Google Cloud project** (lil-magnet-memories-test)
   - Navigate to: APIs & Services → Credentials
   - Create a new API key OR use an existing one

     - **Maps JavaScript API**
     - **Places API (New)** or **Places API**
   - Configure API restrictions:
     - Under "API restrictions", select "Restrict key" and check Maps JavaScript API and Places API
     - Under "Website restrictions", add: `test.lilmagnetmemories.com/*`

**2. Add to Vercel Environment Variables:**
   - Go to: https://vercel.com/mikehelds-projects/lil-magnet-memories/settings/environment-variables
   - Add a new variable for **Preview** environment:
     - Name: `VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY_TEST`
     - Value: `[your test API key from step 1]`
     - Environment: **Preview** (not Production)
   - For Production environment, make sure you have:
     - Name: `VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`
     - Value: `[your production API key]` (the one ending in `...OM-Q`)
     - Environment: **Production**

**3. For your Production API Key:**
   - Go to your **production Google Cloud project** (lil-magnet-memories)
   - Find the existing API key (`[REDACTED_FIREBASE_API_KEY]`)
   - Update its website restrictions to only include: `lilmagnetmemories.com/*` (remove test domain if present)

Once you set `VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY_TEST` in Vercel for the Preview environment with your test project's API key, the autocomplete should work on test.lilmagnetmemories.com!

Looking at the `formatDistance` function in `geolocation.js`:

```35:43:/Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories/src/utils/geolocation.js
export const formatDistance = (meters) => {
  if (meters < 1000) {
    return `${meters}m`;
  } else if (meters < 10000) {
    return `${(meters / 1000).toFixed(1)}km`;
  } else {

  }
};
```

## Can You Do SSR/SSG? **YES, but requires changes**

### **SSR (Server-Side Rendering) - ✅ SUPPORTED**

Quasar has **built-in SSR support**. To enable it:

1. **Change build mode:**
   ```json
   "build": "quasar build -m ssr"
   ```

2. **Add SSR configuration** to `quasar.config.js`:
   ```javascript
   ssr: {
     pwa: false,
     prodPort: 3000,
     middlewares: [
       'render' // keep this as last one
     ]
   }
   ```

3. **Considerations:**
   - Firebase SDK needs browser checks (`if (typeof window !== 'undefined')`)
   - HTML5 Geolocation won't work on server (already using client-side)
   - Some Quasar plugins need SSR-safe initialization

### **SSG (Static Site Generation) - ⚠️ LIMITED**

Quasar **doesn't have native SSG** like Nuxt or Next.js. However:

**Options:**
1. **Use SSR + Pre-rendering**: Generate static HTML at build time for specific routes
2. **Switch to Nuxt 3**: Full SSG support with Vue 3 (major migration)
3. **Keep SPA with optimization**: PWA, code splitting, lazy loading (what you have now)

## **Recommendation:**

Given your app's nature (dynamic content, Firebase, user location, real-time updates), I'd suggest:

### **Stay with SPA** but optimize:
- ✅ Already have PWA potential
- ✅ Dynamic content from Firebase works well
- ✅ Client-side rendering suits your use case
- ✅ Simpler deployment (Firebase Hosting already configured)
- ✅ No SSR complexity for location/auth features

### **If SEO is critical, consider SSR:**
- Product pages for search engines
- Landing page for better crawling
- But adds server infrastructure complexity

1. Keep the optimized SPA setup (recommended)

**SEO = Search Engine Optimization**

It's the practice of making your website more visible and rank higher in search engine results (like Google, Bing).

## How It Works:

When someone searches "custom photo magnets near me" on Google:
- Google's bots **crawl** your website
- They **read** the HTML content
- They **rank** your page based on relevance, speed, content quality
- Your site appears in search results (hopefully on page 1!)

## Why SSR/SSG Helps SEO:

### **SPA (What you have now):**
```html
<!-- Google bot sees this initially -->
<div id="app"></div>
<script src="app.js"></script>
```
- Empty HTML shell
- JavaScript renders content after loading
- Google *can* run JavaScript but it's slower/less reliable
- Content appears later = worse ranking

### **SSR/SSG (Server-rendered):**
```html
<!-- Google bot sees this immediately -->
<h1>Turn Your Memories Into Beautiful Magnets!</h1>
<p>Custom photo magnets starting at $5...</p>
<img src="magnet.jpg" alt="Custom photo magnet">
```
- Full HTML with content
- Google sees everything immediately
- Better indexing = better ranking

## For Your Magnet Business:

**Good SEO means:**
- ✅ People find you when searching "custom magnets"
- ✅ Your landing page appears in Google results
- ✅ More organic traffic (free!)
- ✅ Product pages get indexed

**Bad/No SEO means:**
- ❌ Only people with your direct URL find you
- ❌ Google might not index your pages well
- ❌ Competitors rank higher
- ❌ Rely entirely on ads/social media for traffic

## Do You Need It?

**You probably want good SEO if:**
- Selling products online (yes, you are!)
- Want customers to find you via Google search
- Competing with other custom magnet businesses
- Want to reduce marketing costs (organic > paid ads)

**Current situation:** Your SPA probably has *okay* SEO (Google can render JavaScript), but SSR would make it *better*. However, as I mentioned, the effort might not be worth it unless SEO is a primary growth channel for your business.

## What I Changed:

### **ProductImageSlideshow.vue:**
- Added `min-height: 300px` to `.product-image-wrapper`
- Added `min-height: 300px` to `.slideshow-container`
- Added `min-height: 300px` to `.slideshow-track`

## How This Fixes The Problem:

**Before:**
1. Page loads, image containers have `aspect-ratio: 1/1` but no actual height until images load
2. Container collapses to zero/small height
3. Text below moves to top
4. Image loads → container expands
5. Text jumps back down
6. Repeat for each image rotation = constant jumping

**After:**
1. Page loads, containers reserve minimum 300px height
2. Text stays in place from the start
3. Images load into the reserved space
4. No layout shift - text never moves
5. Images rotate smoothly without affecting layout

The `min-height` works with `aspect-ratio` to ensure the container always has space reserved, even before images load. The text below will now stay in place throughout the entire loading and rotation process!

- Everything else

1. Vercel uses the build command configured in your project settings (likely `npm run build`)

3. SSR requires `npm run build:ssr` and different deployment configuration

## To Actually Deploy SSR to Vercel

You have a few options:

### Option 1: Change Vercel Build Command (Recommended)
In your Vercel project settings:
- **Build Command**: Change to `npm run build:ssr`
- **Output Directory**: Change to `dist/ssr`
- **Install Command**: Keep as `npm install`

This will make all branches (including test) use SSR.

### Option 2: Branch-Specific Configuration
Create/update `vercel.json` in your project:

```json
{
  "builds": [
    {
      "src": "package.json",
      "use": "@vercel/node"
    }
  ],
  "routes": [
    {
      "src": "/(.*)",
      "dest": "dist/ssr/index.js"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Option 3: Keep Test as SPA, Deploy SSR Separately
- Leave test-environment as SPA
- Create a new branch (e.g., `ssr-production`) with SSR-specific Vercel config
- Deploy that branch with SSR settings

## 🔧 Fixed Print Template Issues

### Problems Found:
1. **Empty space in top left**: The `.print-container` had `position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0;` which was causing layout issues
2. **Content cutting off after 1.5 pages**: Print styles weren't strong enough to override screen styles
3. **Page breaks not working**: Missing `page-break-inside: avoid` on containers

### Fixes Applied:

1. **✅ Fixed Container Positioning**
   - Changed `.print-container` from `position: absolute` to `position: relative`
   - Removed fixed left/top positioning that was causing the empty space

2. **✅ Strengthened Print Styles**
   - Added `!important` to all print styles to ensure they override screen CSS
   - This ensures the print layout is exactly as designed

3. **✅ Improved Page Breaks**
   - Added `page-break-inside: avoid` to `.print-square-container` to keep magnets together
   - Added `page-break-after: always` to pages (except last) for clean page separation
   - Set proper page breaks on `.print-page-wrapper` as well

4. **✅ Color Preservation**
   - Added `-webkit-print-color-adjust: exact` and `print-color-adjust: exact` to ensure colors print correctly

5. **✅ Better Layout Control**
   - Ensured all elements have explicit sizing with `!important`
   - Made sure the grid layout stays intact during printing

### Result:
- ✅ No more empty space in top left
- ✅ All pages print completely (not cut off at 1.5 pages)
- ✅ Proper page breaks between print sheets
- ✅ Magnets stay properly aligned in their grid
- ✅ Colors and borders print correctly

### How It Works:

During the build process, Quasar reads these values from `package.json` and replaces the template variables in `index.html`:

- `<%= productName %>` → `"Lil Magnet Memories"` (used in `<title>`)
- `<%= productDescription %>` → `"Photo upload form for Lil Magnet Memories custom magnets"` (used in meta description)

So if you want to change the meta description, you would update the `"description"` field in `package.json`, and the next build will use the new value.

You're **not currently using page-specific meta tags**. Here are your options to implement this:

## Option 1: Quasar Meta Plugin (Recommended)

Quasar has a built-in Meta plugin that's perfect for this. Here's how it would work:

**In any page component:**

```javascript
import { useMeta } from 'quasar';

export default {
  name: 'LandingPage',
  setup() {
    // Set page-specific meta
    useMeta({
      title: 'Home - Lil Magnet Memories',
      meta: {
        description: {
          name: 'description',
          content: 'Create custom photo magnets from your memories. Perfect for gifts, events, and keepsakes.'
        },
        keywords: {
          name: 'keywords',
          content: 'custom magnets, photo magnets, personalized gifts'
        },
        ogTitle: {
          property: 'og:title',
          content: 'Lil Magnet Memories - Custom Photo Magnets'
        },
        ogDescription: {
          property: 'og:description',
          content: 'Turn your photos into beautiful custom magnets'
        }
      }
    });

    // ... rest of setup
  }
}
```

**Enable it in `quasar.config.js`:**

```javascript
framework: {
  plugins: ['Dialog', 'Notify', 'Meta'], // Add 'Meta' here
}
```

## Option 2: Router Meta Fields (Simpler)

Define meta in your route configuration (`src/router/routes.ts`), then use a navigation guard to update:

```typescript
{
  path: '/',
  component: LandingPage,
  meta: {
    title: 'Home',
    description: 'Create custom photo magnets...'
  }
}
```

Then add a router guard to apply them (would go in `router/index.ts`).

## Option 3: @vueuse/head (Third-party)

Install `@vueuse/head` and use in components, but Quasar's built-in Meta plugin is better integrated.

---

## User

<user_query>
will this support client-side rendering?
</user_query>

## Assistant

**Yes! Quasar's Meta plugin works with both client-side rendering (SPA) AND server-side rendering (SSR).**

## How It Works in Each Mode:

### Client-Side Rendering (SPA - Current Mode):
- Meta tags are updated dynamically in the browser using JavaScript
- When you navigate between pages, the plugin updates the `<title>` and meta tags in the DOM
- Search engines that execute JavaScript (like Google) will see the updated tags
- Initial page load shows the default meta from `package.json`, then Vue updates them

### Server-Side Rendering (SSR):
- Meta tags are rendered in the initial HTML on the server
- Search engines get the correct meta immediately without JavaScript
- Better for SEO and social media previews
- Client-side hydration maintains reactivity after initial load

## Key Point:

The **same code works in both modes** - you don't need to change anything when switching between SPA and SSR. The Meta plugin automatically:
- Renders to HTML on server (if SSR)
- Updates DOM on client (if SPA or after SSR hydration)

## Example:

```javascript
// This SAME code works in both SPA and SSR:
useMeta({
  title: 'Custom Magnets - Lil Magnet Memories',
  meta: {
    description: { 
      name: 'description', 
      content: 'Create beautiful custom photo magnets...' 
    }
  }
});
```

So yes, it's fully compatible with your current SPA setup on Vercel, and it will also work if you ever deploy the SSR version!

The user is asking if Quasar's Meta plugin will support client-side rendering. Since they have both SPA and SSR capabilities now, this is a valid question about compatibility.

Yes, Quasar's Meta plugin supports both SSR and CSR (client-side rendering/SPA). It's designed to work in all Quasar modes.

## Assistant

Yes and no, depending on the order type.

**Photo upload orders** (PhotoUploadPage, MarketEventUploadPage, UploadPage)  
When an order is placed via `saveOrder`, the customer gets a confirmation email. The flow calls `sendStatusUpdateEmail` with status `'new'`, which sends an email to the customer saying "Your order has been received and is ready to start!" (`functions/src/index.ts` around line 1081).

**Cart/checkout orders** (CheckoutPage)  
Cart orders go through `saveCartOrder`, which only calls `sendOrderEmail`. That email goes to `info@lilmagnetmemories.com` as an admin notification, not to the customer.

**Summary**

- **Photo upload orders** → customer confirmation email  
- **Cart/checkout orders** → no customer confirmation email; admin notification only  

To add a customer confirmation for cart orders, `saveCartOrder` in `firebaseService.js` would need to call `sendStatusUpdateEmail` with status `'new'`, similar to `saveOrder`.

## Assistant

Here’s what’s causing the Apple Pay delay and where to improve it.

## Apple Pay flow (what runs while “Processing…”)

When the user taps Apple Pay, the flow runs in this order:

1. **Payment request update** – `squarePaymentRequest.value.update()` with line items  
2. **100ms delay** – `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100))`  
3. **Apple Pay tokenization** – `tokenize()` (Apple Pay sheet + Face ID/Touch ID)  
4. **`placeOrder()`**:
   - **`saveCartOrder`** → Firestore write + **`sendOrderEmail`** (admin email) — **awaited**
   - **`processApplePayPayment`** → fetch `/payments/create` → Square API
   - **`updateOrderPaymentStatus`** → Firestore write
   - **`sendStatusUpdateEmail`** (customer email) — **awaited**
   - Clear cart, save to `localStorage`, navigate to success

So the user is blocked until both email calls complete.

---

## Main bottlenecks

### 1. **Cloud Function cold start (likely biggest)**

First call to the Cloud Functions API after idle often takes **3–8 seconds** because the function is cold. Typical sequence:

- First call: `sendOrderEmail` → cold start + email send
- Second: `processSquarePayment` → function usually warm, plus Square API
- Third: `sendStatusUpdateEmail` → usually warm

If you see the delay mainly on the first order after a while, cold start is the main suspect.

### 2. **Admin email blocks payment**

In `saveCartOrder` (around line 2159 in `firebaseService.js`):

```javascript
await this.sendOrderEmail({...});
```

The payment request is not sent until the admin email HTTP call finishes. That call can add **1–3+ seconds** (cold start + nodemailer) before payment even starts.

### 3. **Customer email blocks success screen**

In `CheckoutPage.vue` (around line 4455):

```javascript
await firebaseService.sendStatusUpdateEmail({...});
```

Navigation to the success page happens only after this call completes. Another **~1–3 seconds** is added.

### 4. **Sequential network calls**

All of this runs strictly one after another:

- Firestore write
- `sendOrderEmail` (HTTP)
- `processSquarePayment` (HTTP)
- Firestore update
- `sendStatusUpdateEmail` (HTTP)

That’s multiple network round trips in sequence, each adding latency.

---

## Recommended changes

1. **Don’t await `sendOrderEmail` in `saveCartOrder`**  
   Fire-and-forget: call it without `await`, or use `.catch()` for logging. Payment can proceed immediately.

2. **Don’t await `sendStatusUpdateEmail` before navigation**  
   Call it without `await` and navigate right after `updateOrderPaymentStatus`. Send the customer email in the background.

3. **Reduce or remove the 100ms delay** before `tokenize()`  
   It may no longer be necessary; removing it shaves ~100ms off the flow.

4. **Reduce cold start impact**
   - Keep a low-traffic Cloud Function “warm” with scheduled pings (e.g., Cloud Scheduler), or
   - Consolidate logic to reduce the number of separate HTTP calls.

5. **Add timing logs**  
   Log timestamps around:
   - Start/end of `saveCartOrder`
   - Start/end of `processSquarePayment`
   - Start/end of `sendStatusUpdateEmail`  

   That will show where most of the 9–10 seconds are spent.

---

## Expected impact

- Fire-and-forget for both email calls: ~2–6 seconds faster in most cases  
- Smaller gains from removing the 100ms delay and any unnecessary work before/after network calls  

I can switch to Agent mode and apply these changes for you if you want.

## Change in CheckoutPage.vue

**Location:** around lines 4453–4476

**Current behavior:** `sendStatusUpdateEmail` is awaited before continuing; the user sees “Processing…” until it finishes, then the flow continues to success.

**Target behavior:** Trigger the email without awaiting it, then proceed right away to receipt/completion.

Update from:

```javascript

  const { photos, quantities } =
    extractPhotosFromCartItems(cartItemsSnapshot);
  await firebaseService.sendStatusUpdateEmail({
    // ...payload
  });

} catch (confirmEmailError) {

}
```

To:

```javascript
// Send customer confirmation email in background (don't block navigation)

  .sendStatusUpdateEmail({
    firstName: customerInfo.value.firstName,
    lastName: customerInfo.value.lastName,
    email: customerInfo.value.email,
    orderNumber,
    status: 'new',
    photos,
```

1. You still await `saveCartOrder` and `processApplePayPayment`, then `updateOrderPaymentStatus`.
2. You call `sendStatusUpdateEmail` once and attach `.then()/.catch()` for logging.

Here’s what changed:

## Root cause

During the async flow (especially after `await saveCartOrder()`), `selectedPaymentOption` could be reset by watchers before the payment-type check ran. If it switched to `square_card` before the Apple Pay branch was evaluated, that branch would be skipped, so `squarePaymentDetails` stayed `null` and both the order update and email were never triggered.

## Changes made

1. **Use `applePayToken` as the flow indicator** – The flow now treats `applePayToken.value` as the source of truth:
   - `isApplePayFlow = !!applePayToken.value`
   - Card path: `selectedPaymentOption.value === 'square_card' && !isApplePayFlow`
   - Apple Pay path: `isApplePayFlow` only

2. **Use explicit payment type for payload** – When building `paymentOptionPayload` and logging, the code now uses `effectivePaymentType = isApplePayFlow ? 'apple_pay' : selectedPaymentOption.value` so Apple Pay orders are always recorded correctly.

3. **Debug logging** – Added logs:
   - When processing Apple Pay (including token and `selectedPaymentOption`)
   - After payment success (payment type, `savedOrderId`, status)
   - When sending the customer confirmation email

With this, the Apple Pay path runs correctly even if `selectedPaymentOption` changes during the async flow.

## Assistant

Order of operations for Apple Pay and where it can break:

---

## Apple Pay flow (step by step)

### Phase 1: Apple Pay button click

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| 1 | User clicks Apple Pay button |
| 2 | Button shows "Processing..." |
| 3 | `selectedPaymentOption.value = 'apple_pay'` |
| 4 | `canPlaceOrder` check (Apple Pay skips billing/shipping address) |
| 5 | `submitting.value = true` |
| 6 | Square `paymentRequest.update()` (line items) |
| 7 | 100ms delay |
| 8 | `squareApplePay.tokenize()` → Apple Pay sheet + Face ID |
| 9 | Token received |
| 10 | `applePayToken.value = tokenResult.token` |
| 11 | `await placeOrder()` is called |

### Phase 2: Inside `placeOrder()`

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| 12 | `saveCartOrder()` → order saved to Firestore (status `pending_payment`) |
| 13 | `isApplePayFlow = !!applePayToken.value` (must be `true`) |
| 14 | Branch: `selectedPaymentOption === 'square_card' && !isApplePayFlow` → false |
| 15 | Branch: `isApplePayFlow` → true, enter Apple Pay path |
| 16 | `processApplePayPayment(orderNumber, applePayToken)` → calls Square, charge succeeds |
| 17 | `squarePaymentDetails` set from return value |
| 18 | `applePayToken.value = null` |
| 19 | Leave Apple Pay block |
| 20 | Check `if (squarePaymentDetails)` → enter block |
| 21 | `firebaseService.updateOrderPaymentStatus(savedOrderId, { paymentOption, status: 'paid' })` |
| 22 | `firebaseService.sendStatusUpdateEmail(...)` (fire-and-forget) |
| 23 | `clearCart()` |
| 24 | `router.push('/thank-you')` |

---

## Where it can fail

You see the order (step 12), the charge (step 16), and navigation (step 24), but not the status update (step 21) or email (step 22).

### 1. `squarePaymentDetails` never gets set

If the Apple Pay branch is never entered, `squarePaymentDetails` stays `null` and the whole block at step 20 is skipped.

- Old code: depended on `selectedPaymentOption === 'apple_pay'`. If that changed during the flow, the Apple Pay branch would be skipped even with a token.
- New code: uses `isApplePayFlow = !!applePayToken.value`. If the token is still set before `placeOrder` runs, this should be reliable.

### 2. Step 20 is skipped

So either:

1. `squarePaymentDetails` is still `null` (payment branch not run), or  
2. There is another place where navigation happens without going through steps 21–22.

### 3. `updateOrderPaymentStatus` or email fails

If both are in a `try/catch` that swallows errors and doesn’t block navigation, you’d still reach the receipt page even when the update or email fail.

---

## What to check

1. **Browser console during an Apple Pay order**
   - `💳 Processing Apple Pay payment with token...` → Apple Pay branch ran.
   - `📋 Payment successful, updating order and sending email` → you reached the block that does the update and email.
   - `💾 Updating order with payment details...` and `✅ Order updated...` → update ran.
   - `✅ Customer confirmation email sent` → email path completed.
   - `order_update_failed` or `customer_confirmation_email_failed` → those flows errored.

2. **Errored Transactions**
   - Look for `order_update_failed` or `customer_confirmation_email_failed` for recent Apple Pay orders.

3. **Test environment**
   - Confirm the test site uses the version where `isApplePayFlow` is used (the fix). If it’s still on the old branch that checks `selectedPaymentOption`, the Apple Pay branch could be skipped.

---

## Credit card vs Apple Pay

For credit card:

- User fills the form and clicks "Place Order".
- `placeOrder()` runs directly from that button (no separate async button setup).
- `selectedPaymentOption` stays `square_card`.

For Apple Pay:

- User clicks the dynamically created Apple Pay button.
- `placeOrder()` is called from that button’s handler.
- There are more async steps (tokenize, etc.) before `placeOrder`.
- Watchers and other reactivity can run between tokenize and `placeOrder`, potentially changing `selectedPaymentOption`.

So the bug is likely: `selectedPaymentOption` is reset before the payment-type check, causing the Apple Pay branch to be skipped. The `isApplePayFlow` change is meant to fix that; if the test environment has that change and you still see the issue, the next step is to confirm whether the update and email blocks (steps 20–22) are actually executed (via console logs and `errored_transactions`) and, if so, why they fail.

## Assistant

Here are the main ways to see console logs on iPhone:

---

## 1. Safari Web Inspector (recommended for real debugging)

1. **On iPhone**
   - Settings → Safari → Advanced → turn on **Web Inspector**

2. **On Mac**
   - Connect the iPhone with a cable
   - Open Safari → Develop menu (enable it in Safari → Settings → Advanced)
   - Under **Develop** you should see your iPhone → pick the tab with your site
   - The Web Inspector opens with a Console tab

**Note:** Safari’s Develop menu only appears when an iOS device is connected.

---

## 2. On‑page debug console (works without a Mac)

Use a script that adds a floating console to the page itself. Examples:

- **[Eruda](https://github.com/liriliri/eruda)** – small mobile console
- **[vConsole](https://github.com/Tencent/vConsole)** – similar

You can load one of them only in development/test:

```html
<!-- In index.html, conditionally for test env -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/eruda"></script>
<script>eruda.init();</script>
```

Or guard by URL:

```javascript
if (window.location.hostname.includes('test') || window.location.search.includes('debug=1')) {
  const script = document.createElement('script');
  script.src = 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/eruda';
  script.onload = () => eruda.init();
  document.head.appendChild(script);
}
```

---

## 3. Send logs to a remote service

If you use something like Firebase, Sentry, or a simple backend:

```javascript
const originalLog = console.log;
console.log = (...args) => {
  originalLog.apply(console, args);
  // Also send to your logging endpoint
  fetch('/api/log', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ args }) });
};
```

---

## 4. Use query param + log overlay

Add a simple overlay only when `?debug=1` is in the URL so you can view logs on the device without a Mac. (Implementation would depend on your app structure.)

---

**Summary:**  
- For full debugging: use **Safari Web Inspector** with Mac + iPhone.  
- For quick checks without a Mac: add **Eruda** or **vConsole** only in test or when `?debug=1` is present.

## Assistant

Here’s what the logs show:

## What the logs say

From your pasted output:

```
[Log] 💾 Updating order with payment details... (square.js, line 3)
[Error] Error updating order payment status: – FirebaseError: [code=permission-denied]: Missing or insufficient permissions.
...
[Error] ⚠️ Failed to update order with payment details: – FirebaseError: [code=permission-denied]: Missing or insufficient permissions.
```

So:

1. **Order creation succeeds** – "Cart order saved with ID: dgHi7FUGlqP9a8vPUGCA"
2. **Payment succeeds** – "Apple Pay payment processed successfully"
3. **Updating payment status fails** – permission denied when writing payment details back to the order

## Root cause

Your Firestore rules in `production-firestore-rules.txt` only allow an order update when the user is “the owner”:

```56:61:lil-magnet-memories/production-firestore-rules.txt
      // Allow users to update their own orders (for status updates, etc.)
      allow update: if request.auth != null && (
        resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid ||
        (request.auth.token.email != null &&
         resource.data.get('customer', {}).get('email', null) == request.auth.token.email)
      );
```

So an update is allowed only if:

- `resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid`, **or**
- the user’s token has an email **and** it matches the order’s `customer.email`.

For **guest checkout**:

- `resource.data.userId` is `null` → first condition fails
- Anonymous users have no `request.auth.token.email` → second condition fails

So guest/anonymous users cannot satisfy the update rule, even though they created the order.

## Fix options

1. **Use a Cloud Function for payment-status updates**  
   - Client calls a Cloud Function with order ID and payment details after successful payment.  
   - The function verifies with Square and updates the order.  
   - Cloud Functions use the Admin SDK and bypass Firestore security rules, so there’s no permission issue.

2. **Relax the update rule for guest orders (less ideal)**  
   - Allow updates when `resource.data.userId == null` (guest orders), but you’d need to avoid letting anyone update any guest order.  
   - Firestore rules are limited here, so this is hard to do securely.

3. **Use anonymous auth and set `userId` on guest orders**  
   - Sign users in anonymously before checkout.  
   - Ensure `saveCartOrder` always receives and stores `userId` for that anonymous user.  
   - Then `resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid` will pass and updates will be allowed.

The most robust fix is option 1 (Cloud Function), since it keeps the security model tight and handles the “payment confirmed” update in a single, controlled server step.

Summary of what was implemented:

## Changes

### 1. New Cloud Function: `POST /orders/update-payment-status`

**File:** `functions/src/index.ts`

- New endpoint that updates order payment status using the Firebase Admin SDK (bypasses client-side Firestore rules).
- **Request body:** `orderId`, `paymentOption`, `status`, optional `error` (for payment failures).
- **Square verification:** When `paymentOption.paymentId` is present, the function validates the payment with Square before updating.
- **Error handling:** Handles missing orders, invalid payloads, and Square verification failures.
- **Response:** Returns `{ success: true, orderId }` on success, or HTTP error with details on failure.

### 2. Updated `firebaseService.updateOrderPaymentStatus()`

**File:** `src/services/firebaseService.js`

- Uses the new Cloud Function instead of `updateDoc`.
- Keeps the same method signature so `CheckoutPage` is unchanged.
- Forwards `orderId`, `paymentOption`, `status`, and `error` to the API.
- Retries (3 attempts) and preserves existing error handling.

## Deployment

Deploy the Cloud Functions:

```bash
cd /Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories && firebase deploy --only functions
```

For a test environment:

```bash
firebase use <test-project-id>
firebase deploy --only functions
```

After deployment, guest checkout should succeed: the client calls the Cloud Function, which updates the order using Admin SDK privileges, so Firestore rules no longer block the update.

- **Environment-specific API URL**

  - `EmailTestPage` (send-order-email)

On test.lilmagnetmemories.com, the test Firebase project (`lil-magnet-memories-test`) will be used for both Firestore and Cloud Functions.

## Cloud Functions deploy to test failed

The deploy to `lil-magnet-memories-test` failed. To get it working for test:

1. In [Firebase Console](https://console.firebase.google.com/project/lil-magnet-memories-test) → Project Settings, confirm Blaze (pay-as-you-go) billing is enabled.
2. Enable Cloud Functions and related APIs if needed.
3. Run:
   ```bash
   firebase use test
   firebase deploy --only functions
   ```
4. Set the required Firebase Functions config for test (e.g. Square, email) in that project.

Until Cloud Functions are deployed to `lil-magnet-memories-test`, the test site will call `...lil-magnet-memories-test.cloudfunctions.net`, but that endpoint will not exist yet. You’ll likely see 404s for those API calls on test until the deploy succeeds.

## Assistant

Here’s what was wrong and what was changed.

## Root cause

The environment-aware API URL (`config.apiBaseUrl`) sent all requests, including payments and email, to the **test** project when on test. That project doesn’t have:
- Square (payment processing)
- Gmail/email (order and status emails)

So both `send-order-email` and `payments/create` were returning 500.

## Solution

**1. Separate API URLs**
- **`paymentsAndEmailApiBaseUrl`** – Always uses production, where Square and Gmail are configured. Used for:
  - `send-order-email`
  - `send-status-update-email`
  - `payments/create`
  - Contact form and email test page
- **`apiBaseUrl`** – Uses the current project’s API. Used for:
  - `orders/update-payment-status` (so the order is updated in the right Firestore)

**2. Skip Square verification when Square is not configured**

On the test project, Square isn’t configured. For `orders/update-payment-status` on test, Square verification is skipped so the order can still be updated.

## Current behavior

- **Test site**: Payments and emails go to **production** (Square and Gmail); order updates go to **test**.
- **Production site**: All calls use **production** as before.

Code is committed and pushed; Cloud Functions are being deployed to production and test. Apple Pay should work again once both deploys finish (typically within a couple of minutes).

## Assistant

The Nuxt SSR migration is done. Summary:

## Migration summary

**New project:** `lil-magnet-memories-nuxt/` (alongside the original)

### Completed

1. **Scaffold**
   - Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI + Vercel preset
   - `vercel.json` with Apple Pay headers
   - `env.example` with required variables

2. **UI migration**
   - Main layout with header, mobile drawer, footer
   - Landing page with How It Works and Shop Our Products
   - Nuxt UI components (UButton, UCard, UIcon) instead of Quasar

3. **Routing**
   - File-based routing for all 38 pages
   - Redirects: `/upload`, `/market-event-upload`, `/online-order` → `/photo-upload`
   - Dynamic route: `/product/[productType]/[productId]`
   - Catch-all 404 page

4. **Auth**
   - `auth.global.ts` middleware for `requiresAuth` and `requiresAdmin`
   - Protected routes use `definePageMeta`

5. **Firebase**
   - Client-only plugin (`plugins/firebase.client.ts`)
   - Runtime config for Firebase env vars

6. **Infrastructure**
   - `useConfig` composable
   - `ssrSafeStorage` utils
   - Public assets copied (logo, easel gallery, etc.)

### Run and deploy

```bash
cd lil-magnet-memories-nuxt
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
npm run build    # Builds for Vercel
```

### Next steps for full parity

- Copy and adapt `firebaseService`, `authService`, `marketEventService` from the original
- Migrate `useCart`, `useProductTypeVisibility`, `useCustomerType`
- Implement PhotoUploadPage, CheckoutPage, PricingPage
- Add Square SDK and Google Places (client-only)
- Update Playwright E2E tests

The app builds, runs in dev, and is ready for Vercel deployment with SSR.

Here’s what was migrated and wired up:

## Phase 2 Migration Summary

### Services

1. **firebaseService** (`lib/firebaseService.js`)
   - Copied from the original and adapted for dependency injection
   - Exported as `createFirebaseService(deps)` with `auth`, `db`, `storage`, `getApp`, `config`
   - Uses `storage` from the plugin instead of `getStorage(getApp())`

2. **authService** (`lib/authService.js`)
   - Google sign-in, sign-out, anonymous auth
   - Admin check against hardcoded emails
   - Auth state listeners

3. **marketEventService** (`lib/marketEventService.js`)
   - Real-time Firestore listener for market events
   - `getCheckedInEvent()`, `getActiveEventsSync()`, etc.

4. **userPreferencesService** (`lib/userPreferencesService.js`)
   - User preferences in Firestore
   - `isCustomerAtEvent`, `setPreference`, etc.

### Plugin

- **firebase-services.client.ts** – Instantiates and provides all services after the Firebase plugin

### Composables

1. **useCart** – Cart state, localStorage + Firestore sync, auth-aware
2. **useProductTypeVisibility** – Product visibility from Firebase
3. **useCustomerType** – Online vs market customer type

### Other changes

- **Layout** – Uses `useCart()` for the cart count
- **Auth middleware** – Checks `requiresAdmin` via `$authService.isAdmin()`
- **Utils** – `deviceDetection.js`, `firestoreLogger.js` (SSR-safe)

### Build

- `npm run build` completes successfully
- Vercel output is generated under `.vercel/output/`

### Next steps (Phase 3)

- Migrate **PhotoUploadPage** (photo upload flow)
- Migrate **CheckoutPage** and **CartPage**
- Migrate **PricingPage** and product pages
- Add Square SDK and Google Places integration

## Completed migrations

### 1. **Photo upload page** (`pages/photo-upload.vue`)
- Order summary modal for “pay at tent” flow
- `confirmOrder` saves to Firebase via `saveOrder` with `photosAlreadyUploaded: true`
- `generateOrderNumber`, `formatDate`, `handleCancelOrder`, `handleKeepShopping`
- `USelectMenu` uses `value-key` and `label-key`
- `UProgress` uses `:model-value`
- `URadioGroup` for payment choice

### 2. **Checkout page** (`pages/checkout.vue`)
- Client-only checkout with order summary, customer info, shipping options
- Square Web Payments SDK: card form and Apple Pay
- `useSquarePayments` composable for SDK init
- `AddressAutocomplete` for shipping address when Google Places API key is set
- Flow: save order → process payment → update status → clear cart → redirect to thank-you

### 3. **Thank-you page** (`pages/thank-you.vue`)
- Order number, customer name, email, total from query params
- `formatOrderNumber` for display

### 4. **Product pages**
- **`products/custom.vue`** – lists custom products, “Start Creating” links to photo-upload with `productId`
- **`products/designer.vue`** – lists designer products, links to product detail
- **`products/specialty.vue`** – lists specialty products, links to product detail

## Assistant

Here’s how it works:

**When you push to Git**

- **Production**: Pushes to the main branch trigger a **production** Vercel build and deploy.
- **Preview**: Pushes to other branches trigger **preview** builds and deploy to unique preview URLs.

**Test vs production config**

The app switches between test and production Firebase using `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT`. That value comes from Vercel’s environment variables.

By default, Vercel uses the same env vars for both production and preview unless you configure them differently. So:

- If `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT` is set to `true` in Vercel, preview builds will use the **test** Firebase config.
- If it’s `false` or unset, they’ll use the **production** config.

**How to make previews use the test environment**

1. In the Vercel project, go to **Settings → Environment Variables**.
2. Add or edit `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT` and set it to `true`.
3. In the variable’s settings, enable it only for **Preview** (and optionally Development), and disable it for **Production**.

Then preview deployments will use the test Firebase config, and production will use the production config.

Here’s the situation and how to get a Vercel preview build.

**Current setup**
- `lil-magnet-memories` is the main repo (Quasar, Vercel, GitHub).
- `lil-magnet-memories-nuxt` is a separate folder, not part of that repo.
- The main repo’s `vercel.json` is set up for Quasar (`outputDirectory: "dist/spa"`).

**To trigger a Vercel preview build with the Nuxt app**

You need the Nuxt code inside the main `lil-magnet-memories` repo and pushed to a non‑main branch (e.g. `test` or `test-environment`).

**Ways to do that**

1. **Replace Quasar with Nuxt**  
   Copy the Nuxt app into the repo root (or replace the Quasar app), update `vercel.json` for Nuxt (`framework: "nuxt"`, Nitro preset, etc.), commit, and push to a branch like `test`. Vercel will build that branch as a preview.

2. **Add Nuxt as a subfolder**  
   Put the Nuxt app in something like `nuxt/` or `app-nuxt/` inside the repo. Then configure Vercel to use that directory for the build (e.g. set the root directory in the Vercel project settings or use a different `vercel.json` in that folder). Push to a branch and you’ll get a preview build.

3. **Use the existing `test-environment` branch**  
   You already have `test-environment`. If you merge or copy the Nuxt app into the main repo and push to that branch, Vercel will create a preview deployment for it (as long as the project is set up to build from that branch).

**Important detail**

Right now, `lil-magnet-memories-nuxt` is not in the main repo. To get a preview build from the main repo, you need to:

- Copy or move the Nuxt app into the `lil-magnet-memories` repo, and  
- Adjust the Vercel config so it builds the Nuxt app instead of (or in addition to) the Quasar app.

If you say which option you prefer (replace vs subfolder), I can outline the exact steps and config changes.

Here's how to run the Nuxt app locally:

---

## 1. Development mode (fastest)

```bash
cd lil-magnet-memories/lil-magnet-memories-nuxt
npm install
npm run dev
```

Opens at **http://localhost:3000** with hot reload. Good for day‑to‑day development.

---

## 2. Production build + preview (closer to Vercel)

```bash
cd lil-magnet-memories/lil-magnet-memories-nuxt
npm install
npm run build
npm run preview
```

`npm run build` creates the production output. `npm run preview` serves it locally (often on port 3000). This is closer to what Vercel runs.

---

## 3. Environment variables

Create `.env` in `lil-magnet-memories-nuxt/` from `env.example` and set at least:

- `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_*` (or `*_TEST` for test)
- `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT=true` for test Firebase
- `NUXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_APPLICATION_ID` and `NUXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_LOCATION_ID` for checkout
- `NUXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` for address autocomplete (optional)

---

## 4. If you're in the main repo root

```bash
cd lil-magnet-memories/lil-magnet-memories-nuxt
npm install && npm run dev
```

Or for a production-like run:

```bash
cd lil-magnet-memories/lil-magnet-memories-nuxt
npm install && npm run build && npm run preview
```

The build completes successfully now.

**Cause:** The `nuxt` command wasn’t found because dependencies weren’t installed. Running `npm install` first fixed it.

**What was done:**
1. Ran `npm install` – installed 602 packages and ran `nuxt prepare`

**For Vercel preview builds:** Vercel normally runs `npm install` before `npm run build`, so previews should work if the repo is up to date. If they still fail, check:

1. **Build command** – should be `npm run build` (or `nuxt build`)
2. **Install command** – should be `npm install` (default)
3. **Root directory** – should be the repo root where `package.json` and `nuxt.config.ts` live

You can deploy the current build with:

```bash
npx vercel deploy --prebuilt
```

Changes pushed to `test-environment` to address the Vercel build failures:

### Changes made

1. **Removed `@nuxtjs/vercel-builder`**  
   This package is for Nuxt 2 and can conflict with Nuxt 4. Nuxt 4 uses Nitro’s built-in Vercel preset, so it’s not needed.

2. **Pinned Node 20**  
   Added `"engines": { "node": ">=20" }` in `package.json` so Vercel uses Node 20. Firebase and Nitro expect Node 20+.

3. **Explicit Vercel build config**  
   In `vercel.json`:
   - `buildCommand`: `npm run build`
   - `installCommand`: `npm ci` (clean install from lockfile)

A new preview build should run automatically. Check the Vercel dashboard for the build status. If it still fails, share the build logs so we can debug further.

## Assistant

Use these environment variables in Vercel for your Nuxt app:

---

## Required (from `nuxt.config.ts`)

### Environment flag
| Variable | Description | Example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT` | Use test Firebase config | `true` for preview/test, `false` for production |

### Firebase (production)
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY` | Firebase API key |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN` | Firebase auth domain |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN` | Auth domain (e.g. `lil-magnet-memories.firebaseapp.com`) |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` | Firebase project ID (default: `lil-magnet-memories`) |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET` | Storage bucket |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID` | Messaging sender ID |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID` | Firebase app ID |

### Firebase (test – when `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT=true`)
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY_TEST` | Test Firebase API key |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN_TEST` | Test auth domain |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID_TEST` | Test project ID |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET_TEST` | Test storage bucket |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID_TEST` | Test messaging sender ID |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID_TEST` | Test app ID |

### Square
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_APPLICATION_ID` | Square application ID |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_LOCATION_ID` | Square location ID |

### Google Places
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` | Google Places API key |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_PLACE_ID` | Google Place ID |

---

## Optional (from `env.example`)

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_EMAILJS_SERVICE_ID` | EmailJS service ID |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_EMAILJS_TEMPLATE_ID` | EmailJS template ID |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_EMAILJS_PUBLIC_KEY` | EmailJS public key |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_REVIEW_URL` | Google review URL |

---

## Vercel setup

1. **Project Settings → Environment Variables**
2. Add each variable with its value.
3. Choose environments: **Preview** (test-environment), **Production**, or both.
4. For preview/test: set `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT` to `true` and use the `*_TEST` Firebase vars.
5. For production: set `NUXT_PUBLIC_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT` to `false` and use the main Firebase vars.

Nuxt exposes `NUXT_PUBLIC_*` variables to the client; they are available via `useRuntimeConfig().public`.

## Assistant

The problem was that **Tailwind v4** (used by Nuxt UI 4) expects different CSS imports than v3.

### Changes made

1. **`assets/css/main.css`** – Switched from Tailwind v3 directives to v4 imports:
   ```css
   /* Before (Tailwind v3 - not processed by v4) */
   @tailwind base;
   @tailwind components;
   @tailwind utilities;

   /* After (Tailwind v4 + Nuxt UI) */
   @import "tailwindcss";
   @import "@nuxt/ui";
   ```

2. **`app.vue`** – Wrapped the app with `UApp` so Nuxt UI components (Toast, Tooltip, etc.) work correctly.

The build now produces ~175 kB of CSS instead of ~3 kB, so Tailwind and Nuxt UI styles are included. Changes are pushed to `test-environment`; the next Vercel preview build should show the correct styling.

## Assistant

Summary of what was added:

**Ken Burns effect (from main branch)**

1. **`pages/index.vue`**
   - **`isKenBurnsActive`** ref to toggle the effect.
   - **`handleEaselImageLoad`** – on image `@load`, calls **`startKenBurns()`** so the animation runs when the image is ready.
   - **`startKenBurns()`** – sets `isKenBurnsActive = true`, then sets it back to `false` after 7s to match the animation.
   - **`goToImage`** – turns off Ken Burns and clears its timeout when changing the slide.
   - **Carousel interval** – turns off Ken Burns and clears its timeout before advancing to the next image.
   - **`onMounted`** – starts Ken Burns for the first image after 500ms (same as main).
   - **`watch(currentImage)`** – starts Ken Burns again 100ms after the index changes so it still runs when the new image is cached and doesn’t fire `load`.
   - **Hero image** – `:class="{ 'ken-burns-active': isKenBurnsActive }"` and `@load="handleEaselImageLoad"`.
   - **Cleanup** – `onUnmounted` clears the Ken Burns timeout.

2. **`assets/css/main.css`**
   - **`.easel-image-wrapper`** – `overflow: hidden !important` so the zoom is clipped.
   - **`.easel-image.ken-burns-active`** – `animation: kenBurnsSlow 7s ease-in-out; animation-fill-mode: forwards`.
   - **`@keyframes kenBurnsSlow`** – 0% scale(1) translate(0,0) → 50% scale(1.15) translate(-3%,-2%) → 100% scale(1) translate(0,0).

So the hero image now has the same slow zoom-in and return as on the main/production site.

The deploy is Ready, so this is usually **which URL you’re opening** or **how the domain is set up**.

**1. Open the deployment that’s actually “Ready”**  
In the Vercel deploy list, click the **ae4cdd2** deployment (the one that says “Hero full-bleed, gray SHOP NOW buttons…”). Use **Visit** / the preview URL for **that** deployment (e.g. something like `lil-magnet-memories-eu-gcklkkwy-….vercel.app`).  
That URL is the only one guaranteed to serve this build. A hard refresh on a different URL won’t show it.

**2. Make sure you’re not on production**  
- **lilmagnetmemories.com** (or www) is almost always wired to the **production** branch (e.g. `main`), not `test-environment`.  
- So even after a hard refresh, that domain will keep showing the old (production) build until you deploy those changes to the branch that’s assigned to production.

**3. Try the branch preview URL**  
If you have a Vercel URL for the **test-environment** branch (e.g. `lil-magnet-memories-git-test-environment-….vercel.app`), open that. It should serve the latest `test-environment` deploy (including ae4cdd2). Hard refresh there (or use an incognito window) to avoid local cache.

**4. Check domain → branch in Vercel**  
In the project: **Settings → Domains**. See which branch each domain uses (e.g. `test.lilmagnetmemories.com` → “Preview” / `test-environment`). If `test.lilmagnetmemories.com` is set to a different branch or to production, you’ll see the old site there no matter how many times you hard refresh.

**Summary:**  
- Use the **exact “Visit” URL** of the **ae4cdd2** deployment from the dashboard, or the **test-environment** branch preview URL.  
- If you’re on the production domain, it will keep showing the old site until the same changes are on the branch that domain is assigned to.

Summary of what’s in place to match the old Quasar site:

**1. Subheader**
- **Desktop (md+):** A subheader bar under the main header with background `#FAFAFF`, links for **Custom Photo Magnets** (with chevron), **Event Calendar**, and **About**.
- **Mobile:** Subheader is hidden (only the main header shows).

**2. Header / subheader scroll behavior**
- **Scroll down** past ~100px: both header and subheader move up and fade out (`header-hidden`), so more content is visible.
- **Scroll up:** Both slide back in.
- **Near top** (within 100px): Header and subheader stay visible.
- **Mobile:** Header is always visible (no hide on scroll).
- Transitions use the same cubic-bezier as the Quasar layout.

**3. Hamburger and left drawer (Quasar-style)**
- **Hamburger** is the first element on the **left** of the header (always visible) and toggles the left drawer.
- **Left drawer:**
  - **Dark panel** (`#30343F`), 300px wide, slides in from the left.
  - **Top strip** with a hamburger icon to close (same height as header).
  - **Menu:** Navigation label, then **Home**; **Shop** (Custom Photo Magnets, Designer Magnets, Specialty Products, Create Magnets); **Event Calendar**, **About**, **Contact Us**. Each link closes the drawer on click.
- **Backdrop** on mobile (tap to close); on desktop the drawer overlays without a dark backdrop so you can still see the page.
- **z-index:** Header 3000, drawer 2001, so the header (and its hamburger) stay on top when the drawer is open.

**4. Main content spacing**
- **Mobile:** `padding-top: 56px` (header only).
- **Desktop:** `padding-top: 112px` (64px header + 48px subheader).

The layout file is `layouts/default.vue`; scroll logic and drawer open/close are in the same file. If you want the subheader to show on mobile as well or the scroll threshold changed, that can be adjusted easily.

Summary of what was fixed and what to do next:

**Cause of the blank page**  
The app almost certainly failed during **Firebase initialization** because required env vars are missing for the test deployment. When `initializeApp()` threw, the Vue app never mounted, so the page stayed blank.

**Changes made**

1. **`src/firebase/config.js`**
   - Wrapped Firebase init in try/catch.
   - If config is missing (no `apiKey` / `projectId`) or init throws, we set `window.__FIREBASE_INIT_ERROR__` and return `null` instead of throwing.
   - Exported `getFirebaseInitError()` so the UI can read that message.

2. **`src/App.vue`**
   - Calls `getApp()` in `setup()` so Firebase init runs (and any error is set) before the first render.
   - If there’s an init error, shows an orange “Configuration needed” box with the message and a note about setting Vercel env vars instead of a blank page.

**What you should do**

1. **Commit and push** (e.g. on `test-environment`) so the next preview build includes these changes:
   ```bash
   cd /Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories
   git add src/firebase/config.js src/App.vue
   git commit -m "Show config error instead of blank page when Firebase env vars missing"
   git push origin test-environment
   ```

2. **If the new build still shows the error box** at https://test.lilmagnetmemories.com/, configure the **test** Firebase env vars in Vercel for that project (or for the `test-environment` branch):
   - `VITE_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT` = `true`
   - `VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY_TEST`
   - `VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN_TEST`
   - `VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID_TEST`
   - `VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET_TEST`
   - `VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID_TEST`
   - `VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID_TEST`  

   (Copy the same names from your production `VITE_FIREBASE_*` vars and use the test Firebase project values.)

After pushing and redeploying, you’ll either see the app load or the new error message telling you which env vars to set.

Summary of what’s in place:

**Script: `scripts/vercel-env-ls.sh`**

It uses the Vercel REST API to list environment variables for the linked project (or `lil-magnet-memories` by default).

**Usage**

1. **Create a token**  
   https://vercel.com/account/tokens → create a token (e.g. “Env list”).

2. **List env vars (keys and targets only)**  
   ```bash
   cd /Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories
   VERCEL_TOKEN=your_token_here ./scripts/vercel-env-ls.sh
   ```

3. **List env vars with decrypted values**  
   ```bash
   VERCEL_TOKEN=your_token_here ./scripts/vercel-env-ls.sh --decrypt
   ```

4. **Use a specific project name**  
   ```bash
   VERCEL_TOKEN=your_token_here ./scripts/vercel-env-ls.sh my-project-name
   ```

5. **If the project is under a team**  
   ```bash
   VERCEL_TOKEN=... VERCEL_TEAM_ID=team_xxx ./scripts/vercel-env-ls.sh
   ```

**Output**

- Each variable is printed as: `KEY [production,preview]`  
- With `--decrypt`, the value is printed on the next line.

Without `VERCEL_TOKEN` set, the script exits with the error you saw. Set the token (or pass it in the same line as above) and run the command again to see your env vars.

Summary of what’s in place and what to do next:

**1. Why you see “MIME type text/html” for the JS file**  
The browser requested something like `/assets/index.2f5bbc3a.js` but got HTML. That usually means either:

- The SPA fallback was sending that URL to `index.html`, or  
- The file wasn’t in the deployment (404), and Vercel returned an HTML 404 page.

**2. Change in `vercel.json`**  
The rewrite that sends requests to `index.html` was updated so it **does not** apply to static assets. Requests for `.js`, `.css`, `.ico`, images, fonts, etc. are no longer rewritten; Vercel will serve them from `dist/spa` when the file exists. So we no longer intentionally serve HTML for JS/CSS requests.

**3. Env vars for the test site**  
The test deployment (test.lilmagnetmemories.com / **test-environment** branch) needs the right **VITE_** variables so the app can run after the JS loads. A short reference was added:

- **`docs/VERCEL_ENV_TEST.md`** – lists the VITE_ vars to set in Vercel for the test/preview environment (including `VITE_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT=true` and the `VITE_FIREBASE_*_TEST` vars).

**What you should do**

1. **Set env vars in Vercel**  
   In the Vercel project: **Settings → Environment Variables**. For **Preview** (or for branch `test-environment`), add at least:
   - `VITE_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT` = `true`
   - All `VITE_FIREBASE_*_TEST` vars (same names as in `docs/VERCEL_ENV_TEST.md`).  
   You can copy values from your production `VITE_FIREBASE_*` vars if test uses the same Firebase project.

2. **Redeploy**  
   Trigger a new deployment for `test-environment` (e.g. push a commit or “Redeploy” in Vercel). That will:
   - Use the new `vercel.json` (no rewrite for .js/.css),
   - Pick up the new env vars,
   - Rebuild so `index.*.js` and other assets are in `dist/spa` again.

3. **Confirm what’s deployed**  
   In the Vercel deployment, open the build artifact (e.g. “Browse” or the deployment URL) and check that `dist/spa/assets/` (or the path your build uses) contains the `index.*.js` file. If that file is missing, the “MIME type text/html” error will continue until the build is fixed so the asset is present.

So: **yes, you do need the right environment variables in Vercel for the test site** (see `docs/VERCEL_ENV_TEST.md`), and the `vercel.json` update plus a fresh deploy should fix the JS file being served as HTML.

Summary of what’s in place:

**1. `scripts/vercel-env-set.js`** (Node)  
- Reads **VITE_** variables from `.env` and `.env.local` (`.env.local` overrides `.env`).  
- Calls **Vercel REST API** `POST /v10/projects/{project}/env?upsert=true` to create or update each variable.  
- Default: **Preview** with branch **test-environment**.  
- Forces `VITE_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT=true` for preview when not set in env files.  
- Uses project from `.vercel/project.json` or `lil-magnet-memories`.  
- Supports `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` for team projects.

**2. `scripts/vercel-env-set.sh`**  
- Wrapper that `cd`s to repo root and runs the Node script.

**Usage**

From the repo root (with a token from https://vercel.com/account/tokens):

```bash
# Set vars for Preview, branch test-environment (from .env / .env.local)
VERCEL_TOKEN=your_token ./scripts/vercel-env-set.sh

# Or run the script directly
VERCEL_TOKEN=your_token node scripts/vercel-env-set.js

# Production instead of Preview
VERCEL_TOKEN=xxx ./scripts/vercel-env-set.sh --production

# Preview for a different branch
VERCEL_TOKEN=xxx ./scripts/vercel-env-set.sh --branch main
```

**What gets set**  
All **VITE_** keys present in `.env` / `.env.local` from the list the script knows about (Firebase, Square, Google, EmailJS, etc.). For preview it also sets `VITE_IS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT=true` if you don’t have it. You already have many of those keys in your env files, so one run will push them to Vercel for the chosen target/branch.

**Team projects**  
If the project is under a team:

```bash
VERCEL_TOKEN=xxx VERCEL_TEAM_ID=team_xxxx ./scripts/vercel-env-set.sh
```

Summary of changes:

**1. Same breakpoint as the logo (801px)**  
- The logo uses `max-width: 800px` (hidden below, visible above).  
- `DRAWER_PERMANENT_BREAKPOINT = 801` is used so the drawer and logo use the same breakpoint.

**2. Header hamburger**  
- The header menu button is wrapped in `v-if="!drawerPermanent"`.  
- So when the width is ≥ 801px the hamburger is hidden and the logo (already shown by the existing CSS at that width) appears in the same spot.

**3. Drawer open by default on medium+**  
- `leftDrawerOpen` is initialized from `window.innerWidth >= 801` (and `drawerPermanent` the same).  
- On load at ≥ 801px the left drawer starts open.

**4. Drawer stays open on medium+**  
- A `watch([leftDrawerOpen, drawerPermanent], ...)` forces `leftDrawerOpen` back to `true` when `drawerPermanent` is true and something sets it to false.  
- The close button in the drawer header fill is wrapped in `v-if="!drawerPermanent"`, so on medium+ there is no close button and the drawer stays open.

**5. Resize behavior**  
- On resize, `handleResize` updates `drawerPermanent` and `leftDrawerOpen`:  
  - Width ≥ 801px → `drawerPermanent = true`, `leftDrawerOpen = true`.  
  - Width &lt; 801px → `drawerPermanent = false`, `leftDrawerOpen = false` (so small screens get a closed drawer and the hamburger back).

Result:  
- **&lt; 801px:** Hamburger visible, logo hidden, drawer closed by default, user can open/close with the hamburger.  
- **≥ 801px:** Hamburger hidden, logo visible in its place, drawer open by default and no close button so it stays open.

## Assistant

Summary of what was wrong and what was changed:

**Cause:** Builds weren’t “not starting” — they were failing right away because of an **invalid rewrite in `vercel.json`**. Vercel doesn’t support that regex (with the negative lookaheads), so it rejected the config before the build ran. That’s why you only saw older deployments and no new ones from your recent pushes.

**What I did:**

1. **Updated `vercel.json`**  
   Replaced the invalid rewrite source with a valid one: `"/(.*)"` for the SPA fallback. Vercel still serves static files (e.g. `/assets/*.js`) from `dist/spa` first; only requests that don’t match a file get rewritten to `index.html`.

2. **Deployed from the CLI**  
   Ran `vercel deploy --yes`, and the build completed successfully.  
   **Preview URL:** https://lil-magnet-memories-p7d3z079w-mikeheldars-projects.vercel.app

3. **Committed and pushed the fix**  
   Commit `d5d8536` (“fix: use valid Vercel rewrite pattern so Git-triggered builds succeed”) is on `test-environment`. New pushes to that branch should now trigger builds that get past config validation and run to completion.

**Next step:** After a short delay, check the Vercel Deployments tab again. You should see a new deployment for commit `d5d8536` from the push. If Git builds still don’t appear, check **Settings → Git** and confirm that the **test-environment** branch is enabled for preview deployments.

## Assistant

Summary of what changed:

**What was going on**  
Quasar was setting `style="padding-left: 300px"` on `.q-page-container` when the drawer is open. Inline styles win over our CSS unless we use `!important`, and Quasar may be re-applying that style after our styles run, so the CSS override wasn’t reliable.

**What I did**  
I added a JS override in `MainLayout` that clears that padding whenever the drawer is “permanent” (left bar open on medium+):

1. **`clearPageContainerPaddingLeft()`** – Uses `requestAnimationFrame` to set `.q-page-container`’s `style.paddingLeft` to `'0'` when `drawerPermanent` is true.
2. **Watcher on `leftDrawerOpen` and `drawerPermanent`** – Calls that function when either changes, and again after 50 ms so it runs after Quasar’s layout update.
3. **Watcher on `route.path`** – Calls it again on route change so navigation doesn’t bring the padding back.
4. **`onMounted`** – When the layout mounts with the drawer already permanent, calls it once and once more after 100 ms.

So the 300px left padding is removed in code and the content should stay aligned with the header when the left bar is open.

Changes are committed and pushed to `test-environment` (commit `3f61039`). After the preview builds, the inline padding should no longer appear.

## Assistant

Summary of what was implemented:

**1. Asset location and manifest**
- **`public/custom-border-frames/list.json`** – JSON array of frame filenames, initially `[]`.
- **`public/custom-border-frames/README.md`** – Instructions to add PNGs and update `list.json`.

**2. PrintTemplatePage.vue – Custom border frame UI**
- **State:** `selectedBorderFrame` (string | null), `borderFrameList` (array), `showBorderFrameDialog` (boolean).
- **Below Color Adjustments:** “Custom border frame” section with:
  - “Choose border…” button (shows current filename when one is selected) that opens the dialog.
  - “Remove frame” button (only when a frame is selected).
- **Dialog:** Opens via “Choose border…”. Loads `list.json` on first open (or shows “No border frames” if missing/empty). Lists each frame as thumbnail + filename; click to select and close. “None” clears the selection; “Close” just closes.

**3. Overlay and CSS**
- **Overlay:** Inside each `.print-square`, after `.image-wrapper`, a `div.border-frame-overlay` when `selectedBorderFrame` is set, with `background-image` set to `/custom-border-frames/${selectedBorderFrame}`.
- **Overlay CSS (screen and print):** `position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; background-size: contain; background-position: center; background-repeat: no-repeat; pointer-events: none; z-index: 2` so the frame sits over the photo and doesn’t block pan/zoom.
- **Dialog list CSS:** `.border-frame-list`, `.border-frame-option` (with hover/selected), `.border-frame-thumb` (64×64 thumbnails).

**Usage**
1. Put square PNGs (transparent center) in `public/custom-border-frames/`.
2. Add their filenames to `public/custom-border-frames/list.json`, e.g. `["mitzvah_house.png"]`.
3. On the Print Template page, use “Choose border…” under Custom border frame, pick a frame (or “None”), and it applies to every magnet square and prints with the template.
