## Assistant

Summary of changes:

**1. Floating toolbar**
- The controls bar is no longer inside the per-page loop. A single **sticky** toolbar is the first child of the print container.
- It sits in a wrapper with `position: sticky; top: 16px; z-index: 10` so when you scroll, the top of the toolbar stays visible.

**2. Collapsible sections**
- **Fine Adjustments** – header + chevron to expand/collapse (default **open**).
- **Color Adjustments** – same behavior, default **closed** so the bar fits on screen.
- **Custom border frame** – same behavior, default **open**.
- Clicking a section header toggles it; the chevron shows expand_less when open and expand_more when closed.

**3. Layout**
- Pages now render in a vertical stack under the single toolbar instead of repeating the bar beside each page. The toolbar stays at the top while you scroll through pages.

**4. CSS**
- `.print-controls-float` – sticky wrapper.
- `.controls-section`, `.controls-section-header`, `.controls-section-body`, `.controls-section-title` – section layout and hover on headers.

If you want the bar on the **left** again (sidebar style) with pages on the right, that can be done with a row layout and the same sticky behavior.

Here’s how to run it locally and open the print template:

**1. Start the dev server**

From the project root:

```bash
cd /Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories
npm run dev
```

(or `yarn dev` if you use Yarn)

That runs **Quasar’s dev server** (usually `quasar dev`). When it’s up, the terminal will show a URL, typically **http://localhost:9000** or **http://localhost:5173** (port can vary).

**2. Open the print template in the browser**

- Go to: **http://localhost:&lt;port&gt;/print-template**  
  (use the port shown in the terminal.)
- The route has `requiresAuth: true` and `requiresAdmin: true`, so you must be **signed in as an admin**. If you’re not, you’ll be redirected to login; sign in with an admin account, then go to `/print-template` again.

**3. See the toolbar**

On the print template page you’ll see the sticky toolbar at the top and the collapsible sections (Fine Adjustments, Color Adjustments, Custom border frame). The page expects order/photo data; you may get there from **Orders** (e.g. “Print” on an order) or **Photo selector** / **Magnet studio** (“Send to print template”) so that photos are loaded. If you open `/print-template` with no order/photo state, the page may load but without photos until you go through one of those flows.

## Assistant

To run **lil-magnet-memories** locally:

**1. Install dependencies** (if you haven’t recently):

```bash
cd /Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories
npm install
```

**2. Start the dev server:**

```bash
npm run dev
```

That runs `quasar dev` using the project’s Quasar CLI from `node_modules`, so you don’t need a global `quasar` install. The terminal will show a URL (often **http://localhost:9000** or **http://localhost:5173**).

**3. Open the app and the print template:**

- In the browser: **http://localhost:&lt;port&gt;** (use the port from the terminal).
- Print template: **http://localhost:&lt;port&gt;/print-template**

**4. Auth for `/print-template`:**

That route uses `requiresAuth: true` and `requiresAdmin: true`. Sign in with an admin account, then go to `/print-template`. You can also get there from **Orders** (e.g. Print on an order) or **Photo selector** / **Magnet studio** (“Send to print template”) so the page has order/photo data.

**If `npm run dev` fails** (e.g. “quasar: command not found”):

- Ensure you’re in the project root and ran `npm install`.
- Try: `./node_modules/.bin/quasar dev` so the CLI is run from the local install.

Summary of changes so the “forward” action (Submit Order / Confirm Order) stays visible on mobile:

**1. PhotoUploadPage.vue (Order Summary dialog)**  
- **Dialog card** (`order-summary-dialog-card`):  
  - `max-height: min(90vh, 85dvh)` so height respects the dynamic viewport.

- **Actions** (`order-summary-dialog-actions`):  
  - `padding-bottom: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` so Cancel, Keep Shopping, and Submit Order sit above the system/browser UI (e.g. iOS home indicator, mobile nav bar).  
- These styles are in an **unscoped** `<style>` block so they still apply when Quasar teleports the dialog to `body`.

**2. MarketEventUploadPage.vue (Order Summary dialog)**  
- Same classes and the same unscoped styles added so the “Confirm Order” (and Cancel) actions get the same safe area and height behavior when used at a live event.

**Result**  
- Buttons stay above the browser bottom bar thanks to safe-area padding.  
- On small screens the dialog is shorter (78vh) so the action bar stays in view without scrolling.  
- `85dvh` / `78vh` keeps the dialog within the visible viewport so the primary action is no longer hidden on mobile.

- **Purchase** (new): outline primary button with “Purchase” and cart icon, placed to the right of View Details in a `product-actions` row.  
- **`goToPurchase(product)`**: `router.push({ path: '/photo-upload', query: { productId: product.id } })` so the upload page opens with that product pre-selected.

Summary of what changed:

1. **No more scrolling inside the easel**
   - `.hero-section` had `overflow-y: auto`, which created a scrollable area. It’s now `overflow-y: visible`, so the whole page scrolls and there’s no separate scroll in the hero/easel.

2. **Easel height on medium/large so dots are in view**
   - On viewports **≥600px**, the easel container uses **max-height: 50vh** instead of 620px, so the image + dots stay within about half the viewport height. That keeps the dots visible without having to scroll the easel.

3. **How it works stays below**
   - How it Works is unchanged in the layout and stays below the easel and dots. With the hero no longer scrolling and the easel shorter on medium+, the dots are in view and How it Works appears when you scroll the page.

Changes are pushed to **test-environment** (commit `dfd4a8d`). You should no longer need to scroll inside the easel to see the dots.

## Assistant

Summary of what changed:

**Cause:** The dots were `position: absolute`, so they were taken out of the document flow. The easel container’s height was then based only on the image. Depending on layout/stacking, the next section (How it Works) could sit over the same vertical space and cover the dots.

**Fix:** The dots are now in the normal document flow:

1. **No more absolute positioning** – Removed `position: absolute`, `top`, `left`, and `transform` from `.easel-carousel-dots` on all breakpoints (including the small-screen override).

2. **Dots as a flex child** – The easel container is a column flexbox: first the image wrapper (`flex: 1`), then the dots (`flex-shrink: 0`). The dots sit directly under the image and take up real space in the layout.

3. **No padding used as “space” for dots** – Removed the easel container’s `padding-bottom` that was only there to make room for the absolutely positioned dots. Spacing comes from the dots’ own `margin: 12px auto 16px auto`.

4. **Image wrapper** – Added `min-height: 0` on the image wrapper so the flex layout can shrink correctly and the dots stay visible.

With this, the hero’s height includes the dots, so the landing container (and How it Works) always start below them and can’t overlap. Pushed to **test-environment** (commit `fec993c`).

## Assistant

Summary of changes:

**1. Total Magnets calculation**
- **Bug:** For orders with `cartItems`, the code did `return order.cartItems.reduce(...)` and never added that value to the running total, so those magnets were missing from the event total.
- **Fix:** Total Magnets now sums magnets from every order:
  - If the order has `totalMagnets`, that value is used.
  - Else if it has `cartItems`, each item’s magnets are counted via `item.quantity ?? item.totalMagnets ?? (item.photos?.length || 0)` and added to the total.
  - Else `order.photos.length` is used if present.
- Numeric values are coerced with `Number()` so the total is correct.

**2. Three cards on one line**
- Replaced fixed `col-4` with a flex row that keeps all three cards on one line: added classes `event-order-cards` and `event-order-card-col`.
- CSS: `event-order-cards` uses `flex-wrap: nowrap !important`; each `event-order-card-col` uses `flex: 1 1 0` and `min-width: 0` so the three cards share space and stay on a single row.

Changes are pushed to **test-environment** (commit `9973d39`).

## Assistant

Summary of what was implemented:

**1. Drawer visibility (MainLayout)**  
- `isOperator` is set from `authService.isOperator()` on auth and cleared on sign-out.  
- `updateDrawerVisibility()` sets `drawerPermanent = (width >= 801) && (isAdmin || isOperator)` and keeps `leftDrawerOpen` in sync.  
- Resize handler and auth paths (including `isAdminAsync`) call `updateDrawerVisibility()`.  
- `isOperator` is returned from `setup()`.

**2. Firebase promo API**  
- **firebaseService.js:**  
  - `getPromoCodes()` – list all, ordered by `createdAt` desc.  
  - `createPromoCode({ code, type, value, validFrom?, validUntil?, active })` – code stored uppercase; doc id = code.  
  - `updatePromoCode(id, fields)` – partial update; dates converted to Firestore `Timestamp` when needed.  
  - `deletePromoCode(id)` – sets `active: false`.  
  - `validatePromoCode(code)` – returns `{ valid, type?, value? }` or `{ valid: false, message }` (active + within date range).  
- **production-firestore-rules.txt:**  
  - `promo_codes/{codeId}`: `read: if true`, `write: if request.auth != null`.

**3. Pricing page – Promo Codes**  
- New “Promo Codes” card with table (code, discount type/value, validity, active, Edit/Delete).  
- “Add Promo Code” opens a dialog: code, type (percent/fixed), value, optional valid from/until (date pickers), active.  
- Edit (code read-only) and Deactivate with confirmation.  
- Validation: code required; value &gt; 0; percent ≤ 100; validUntil &gt; validFrom when both set.  
- `loadPromoCodes()` runs on mount with other admin data.

**4. Checkout**  
- Promo code input + “Apply” (and “Remove” when a code is applied).  
- `applyPromoCode()` calls `validatePromoCode()` and sets `appliedPromoCode` / `appliedPromo`.  
- `promoDiscount` computed: percent = subtotal × (value/100); fixed = min(value, subtotal).  
- `orderTotal` = subtotal + shipping − `promoDiscount`, never negative.  
- Order Total card shows “Promo (CODE): -$X.XX” when applied.  
- Order payload includes `promoCode` and `promoDiscount`; `totalAmount` is the discounted total.

All plan to-dos are done. Optional “subtotalBeforePromo” was not added to the order payload; you can add it later if needed for reporting.

## Assistant

Summary of changes:

**1. Percent off vs dollars (Pricing page)**  
- The type dropdown was binding the whole option object, so the amount field didn’t switch correctly. The select now uses **`emit-value`** and **`map-options`** so the stored value is the string `'percent'`, `'fixed'`, or `'fixed_total'`.  
- The amount field now uses **computed** `promoValueLabel`, `promoValuePrefix`, and `promoValueSuffix`:  
  - **Percent off:** label “Percent (0–100) *”, no `$`, suffix `%`.  
  - **Fixed amount off:** label “Amount off ($) *”, prefix `$`.  
  - **Fixed cart total:** label “Cart total ($) *”, prefix `$`.

**2. Third promo type: Fixed cart total**  
- **Pricing page:** Added a third option “Fixed cart total” (value `fixed_total`). Table shows it as a teal chip “Total $X”. Validation allows `percent`, `fixed`, and `fixed_total`.  
- **firebaseService:** `createPromoCode` and `validatePromoCode` accept and return `type: 'fixed_total'` (with `percent` and `fixed`).  
- **Checkout:** For `fixed_total`, discount is computed so the **order total** (subtotal + shipping) becomes **min(promo value, subtotal + shipping)**. So the customer pays the fixed amount when it’s lower than cart+shipping, otherwise they pay the cart+shipping amount (total never goes above the pre‑promo total).

Files touched:  
`src/pages/PricingPage.vue`, `src/services/firebaseService.js`, `src/pages/CheckoutPage.vue`.

## Assistant

Here’s what’s going on and how to fix it.

**Cause:** The test app uses the Firebase project **lil-magnet-memories-test**. That project’s Firestore rules don’t define the **promo_codes** collection, so `getPromoCodes` and `createPromoCode` get “Missing or insufficient permissions.” Production uses `lil-magnet-memories`, where the rules (and promo_codes) are already deployed.

**Fix:** Deploy the same rules (including promo_codes) to the test project. From the repo root:

```bash
cd /Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories
firebase use lil-magnet-memories-test
firebase deploy --only firestore
```

That deploys `production-firestore-rules.txt` (which already has the promo_codes block) to **lil-magnet-memories-test**. After 1–2 minutes, reload the test site and the Promo Codes section should work.

**Changes made in the repo:**

1. **`tests/test-firestore-rules.txt`**  
   - Added an explicit **promo_codes** block so the test rules file stays in sync with production.

2. **`docs/DEPLOY_TROUBLESHOOTING.md`**  
   - New section: **“Missing or insufficient permissions” for promo codes on test** with:
     - The two commands above to deploy rules to the test project.
     - An alternative: add the promo_codes rules by hand in the [Firestore Rules](https://console.firebase.google.com/project/lil-magnet-memories-test/firestore/rules) UI and publish.

After you run the deploy (or add the rules manually), promo code load/create/edit on the test site should succeed.

## Assistant

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
`position: sticky` was on **each** `.print-controls`, but that block lived **inside** every `print-page-wrapper` in the `v-for`. Sticky only works inside its parent’s scroll range, so the tools “ran out” of room as soon as that page’s row scrolled away.

### Fix
1. **Layout** – One **`.print-workspace`** row: **one** `.print-controls` + **`.print-pages-column`** with all `.print-page-wrapper` / `.print-page` items in the loop.
2. **Sticky** – Same panel stays sticky for the whole print view: `top` is **84px + 8px** (small screens) and **64px + 8px** at **1024px+**, aligned with your `MainLayout` header heights, plus `env(safe-area-inset-top)`.
3. **UX** – `z-index: 100`, `max-height` with **`overflow-y: auto`** so a tall tools panel scrolls inside the sticky column.
4. **≤900px** – Workspace stacks **column**; tools cap at **320px** width so the sheet still fits.
5. **Print** – `@media print` rules added for `.print-workspace` / `.print-pages-column` so layout stays correct; `.print-controls` stays hidden as before.

### Git
Pushed to **`test-environment`**: commit `4f3bffd` — *Print template: single sticky tools column beside all pages (below header)*.

After Vercel finishes deploying, scroll through multiple pages on the print template—the tools column should stay pinned just under the header.

## Assistant

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Why `sticky` didn’t work
Quasar’s layout wraps content in a node that uses **`transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)`**. That creates a new containing block so **`position: sticky` no longer sticks to the viewport** the way you expect—the panel scrolls away with the page.

### What we did instead
1. **`position: fixed`** for the tools panel (class `print-controls--fixed`).
2. An in-flow **`.print-tools-spacer`** (same width as the tools) so the grid still lines up horizontally.
3. **JS** (`updatePrintToolsFixedPosition`) sets **`left`** and **`width`** from the spacer’s `getBoundingClientRect()`, and runs on **scroll** (capture), **resize**, and **`ResizeObserver`** (spacer + panel) so drawer/layout changes stay aligned.
4. **`top`** matches your layout: **`84px + 8px`** on small screens, **`64px + 48px + 8px`** from **768px** up (header + sub-nav, like `MainLayout`).
5. **Narrow (≤900px):** spacer is full width (max **320px**), centered; **`minHeight`** on the spacer matches the fixed panel height so content isn’t covered.
6. **Print:** spacer is hidden with the rest of the no-print UI.

Pushed to **`test-environment`** as commit **`eb08bf4`**. After Vercel deploys, reload the print template and scroll—the tools column should stay under the header.

## Assistant

Yes. Here’s what we’re doing now:

### Horizontal (like before)
`left` and `width` still come from the **in-flow spacer** on every **scroll** (and resize / `ResizeObserver`). So if the main column shifts or the page scrolls horizontally, the tools line up with that column instead of staying glued to the viewport’s left edge.

### Vertical (sticky under header, stop at footer)
We still use **`position: fixed`** (because of Quasar’s `transform` and broken `sticky`), but **`top` is computed each frame**:

1. **Default:** `top` = space under the header (84+8px small, 64+48+8px from 768px up).
2. **Footer:** We read **`.site-footer`**. So the panel’s bottom stays **above the footer** with a **12px** gap:  
   `top = min(preferredUnderHeader, footerTop - gap - panelHeight)`  
   So as the footer moves up, the panel moves up with it instead of covering the footer.
3. **`max-height`** is also capped by the space between the current `top` and the footer (and the viewport), so the inner scroll still fits.

`top` / `max-height` are no longer fixed in CSS; they’re set in JS so this clamping stays correct.

Pushed to **`test-environment`** as **`b05ea0b`**. After deploy, scroll down toward the footer—you should see the tools ride up and stop above it.

## Assistant

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
The frame URL stayed **`/custom-border-frames/rythms_in_bloom.png`**. Browsers and your host’s CDN treat that as the same asset, so they keep serving the **old** file even after deploy and a hard reload.

### Fix (pushed to **`test-environment`**)
1. **`list.json`** now uses a small manifest with a **version** and **frames**:
   - `"v": "2"` → frame URLs become  
     `.../rythms_in_bloom.png?v=2`  
     so caches fetch the new bytes.
2. **`PrintTemplatePage.vue`**
   - Parses both the new object and the **old array** format.
   - **`borderFrameAssetUrl()`** adds `?v=…` when `v` is set.
   - **`fetch(list.json, { cache: 'no-store' })`** so the manifest isn’t stuck in cache.
   - **`loadBorderFrameList()`** runs on **mount** so the version is ready as soon as the page loads.

3. **`README.md`** explains bumping **`v`** whenever you replace a PNG but keep the same name.

After the test build finishes, you should see requests like  
`/custom-border-frames/rythms_in_bloom.png?v=2`.  

**Next time** you swap that PNG again, increment **`v`** in `list.json` (e.g. `"3"`).  

**Production `main`** does not include this yet; merge/cherry-pick when you want it live there too.

## Assistant

### What broke
The build failed on **`PrintTemplatePage.vue` line 344** with Vue’s **`Whitespace was expected`** error. The `:style` binding used **nested template literals and `\"` escapes**, which the **HTML template parser** doesn’t handle, so compilation failed.

### What we did
- Replaced that inline `:style="{ ... }"` with **`:style="borderFrameOverlayStyle(selectedBorderFrame)"`**.
- Added **`borderFrameOverlayStyle()`** in the script so the `url("...")` string is built in JS, not in the template.

`npm run build` completes successfully locally, and the fix is **committed and pushed to `test-environment`** (`695086b`). You can rerun your CI/deploy from there.

### What was wrong
**Production Firestore rules didn’t match what’s in the repo.** The app uses `promo_codes` with:
- **`getDoc`** (checkout)
- **`getDocs` + `orderBy`** (Manage Products list)

If the **live** rules never included `promo_codes` (or still had the old “deny everything else” set), Firestore returns **“Missing or insufficient permissions.”** Products can still work because `products` was already allowed.

### What we did
1. **Deployed** `production-firestore-rules.txt` to **`lil-magnet-memories`** (production) with the Firebase CLI — deploy completed successfully, so **promo rules are live now**.
2. **Tightened the rule text** to spell out **`get, list`** and **`create, update, delete`** for `promo_codes` (same behavior as `read` / `write`, clearer for future you).
3. **Docs + script**: `docs/PRODUCTION_FIRESTORE_RULES.md` now explains this and **`npm run deploy:firestore-rules`** runs `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules`.
4. **Git**: committed and pushed to **`test-environment`** and **`main`** (`dc61cf6`).

Try **Manage Products → Promo codes** again in production (hard refresh if needed). It should load and save.

**Next time** you change `production-firestore-rules.txt`, run:

```bash
firebase use default   # lil-magnet-memories
npm run deploy:firestore-rules
```

(or paste/publish in **Firestore → Rules** in the console).

## Assistant

The app treats you as **at the event** when you’re within **300 meters** of the event’s coordinates.

That’s implemented on the landing page: after computing distance in **meters** (Haversine, rounded), it runs:

```767:775:lil-magnet-memories/src/pages/LandingPage.vue
        // Auto-toggle "at event" if within 300m
        if (distance <= 300) {
          console.log('[Distance] Within 300m - auto-enabling market event mode');
          setCustomerType('market_customer');
        } else {
          console.log('[Distance] More than 300m away - defaulting to online mode');
          // Don't auto-set to online if they're already a market customer
          // Just let them keep their current setting
        }
```

So the threshold is **≤ 300 m** (inclusive). If the event has **no coordinates**, or **location can’t be read**, the code does **not** use distance; it defaults to online and the user can still switch to “at event” manually.

The log explains it: **`"coordinates": null`**.

With **no lat/lng on the event**, the landing page **cannot** run the distance check, so it **never** auto-switches to “at event” / `market_customer`. It explicitly treats that as “we don’t know where the event is” and falls back to online behavior (and your log line about the full event object matches the branch that runs when coordinates are missing).

So people at the venue aren’t failing the 300 m rule — **the geofence path isn’t used at all** until the event has **`coordinates: { lat, lng }`** (whatever shape your admin UI saves).

**What to do**

1. In **Market Events** (or wherever you edit the live event), **set the map / pin / coordinates** for that event so Firestore stores `coordinates`, not only the string `location` (“1738 MacArthur Boulevard…”).
2. After saving, reload the site and check the console again — you should see coordinate logs and then the `Within 300m` logic if GPS is allowed.

**Also worth knowing**

- Users must **allow location** in the browser; if they deny it, the code also won’t auto-set “at event” (it defaults to online).
- Anonymous + `localStorage` for the cart is unrelated to the distance logic; the blocker here is **`coordinates: null`**.

## Assistant

Here’s what the code is actually doing.

### Selecting an address does **not** save coordinates by itself

On the market event form you only bind the string:

```291:297:lil-magnet-memories/src/pages/MarketEventsPage.vue
            <AddressAutocomplete
              v-model="newEvent.location"
              label="Location/Address"
              :rules="[(val) => !!val || 'Location is required']"
              hint="Start typing an address..."
              filled
            />
```

There is **no** `@place-selected` handler on that component in this page.

`AddressAutocomplete` **does** load Google place details and **can** emit coordinates:

```240:253:lil-magnet-memories/src/components/AddressAutocomplete.vue
        const placeData = {
          formattedAddress: place.formatted_address || suggestion.description,
          addressComponents,
          coordinates: place.geometry?.location ? {
            lat: place.geometry.location.lat(),
            lng: place.geometry.location.lng(),
          } : null,
          placeId: suggestion.place_id,
          name: place.name,
        };

        // Emit detailed place information
        console.log('🏗️ [AddressAutocomplete] ✅ Emitting place-selected:', placeData);
        emit('place-selected', placeData);
```

Those coordinates are **not** used by `MarketEventsPage` today.

### Coordinates are set only when **Nominatim** geocoding succeeds

On create/update, the page **re-geocodes** the address string with **`geocodeAddress`** from `geolocation.js`, which calls **OpenStreetMap Nominatim** (not Google):

```113:122:lil-magnet-memories/src/utils/geolocation.js
export const geocodeAddress = async (address) => {
  ...
    const response = await fetch(
      `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=${encodedAddress}&format=json&limit=1`,
```

If that request fails, returns no row, hits policy/rate limits, or errors in the browser, the catch path runs and the event is still saved **with `coordinates: null`**:

```847:850:lil-magnet-memories/src/pages/MarketEventsPage.vue
        } catch (geocodeError) {
          console.warn('[Geocoding] Failed to geocode address:', geocodeError.message);
          // Continue without coordinates - not a critical error
        }
```

So: **yes, you’d expect “pick address → have coords”**, but the app is designed as **“pick address → save text → second geocoder (OSM) → maybe coords”**. Your Firestore doc with `location` set and `coordinates: null` fits **Nominatim failing or not finding a match**, not a bug in the address picker display.

### What to check when debugging

1. **Browser console** when saving the event — look for `[Geocoding] Failed to geocode address:` or network errors to `nominatim.openstreetmap.org`.
2. **Policy / environment** — Nominatim is not really aimed at heavy client-side use; failures from the browser are common enough that this architecture is fragile.

### Better long-term fix (conceptual)

Use the **`place-selected` payload** (Google already has `coordinates`) when creating/updating the event, or geocode with the **same** Google Geocoding/Places flow you already use in the autocomplete—so picking an address reliably sets `coordinates` without depending on a second, separate service.

I’m in **Ask mode**, so I can’t change the code here; if you want that wired up in the repo, switch to **Agent mode** and we can implement it.

## Assistant

Here’s what that log means, in plain terms.

## What happened

1. On **Save**, `MarketEventsPage` calls **`geocodeAddress()`** in `geolocation.js`.
2. That function only talks to **OpenStreetMap Nominatim** (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=...`).
3. For your string  
   `"Scofflaw Brewing Co., MacArthur Boulevard Northwest, Atlanta, GA, USA"`  
   Nominatim returned **no results** → the code throws **`Address not found`** (when `data.length === 0`).
4. The create handler **catches** that error and still creates the event with **`coordinates: null`** (“not a critical error”).

So the address **did** get saved as text; **only** the second step (OSM geocode) failed, so you get **no pin** for distance / “at event.”

## Why Nominatim often fails here

- It’s **not** the same database as Google Places. Long strings with **business names** and US-style addresses are easy for it to miss or treat oddly.
- It can also **rate-limit** or behave inconsistently from the **browser**.
- Your autocomplete already used **Google** and got a good place; the app **does not** use those coordinates today—it only re-geocodes the text with OSM.

## What to do (conceptually)

**Short term (data):** Manually set `coordinates` in Firestore for that event, or edit/save after switching to a geocoder that finds the place (not ideal long term).

**Proper fix (code):** When the user picks a suggestion in `AddressAutocomplete`, **listen for `place-selected`** and save `placeData.coordinates` on the event (Google already returns `geometry`). Optionally keep Nominatim only as a fallback if there’s no place selection.

I’m in **Ask mode**, so I can’t change the repo here. If you switch to **Agent mode**, we can wire `@place-selected` into `MarketEventsPage` (create + edit) so coordinates match the chosen Google place even when Nominatim says “Address not found.”

Here’s what was implemented:

### 1. [`MarketEventsPage.vue`](lil-magnet-memories/src/pages/MarketEventsPage.vue)
- Swapped **`AddressAutocomplete`** for **`GooglePlacesAutocomplete`** on create/edit with **`marketEventPlaceTypes`: `['establishment', 'geocode']`**.
- **`@place-selected`**: stores `{ lat, lng }` in pending state; **`@update:model-value`**: clears a **place**-sourced pin if the address text no longer matches the anchored formatted address (GPS pins are unchanged).
- **Create**: `coordinates` are required — from **manual lat/lng** (if valid), else **pending** (Google pick or **Use my location**). No Nominatim.
- **Edit**: **Manual** or **pending** sets `coordinates`; if the **location string is unchanged**, **`coordinates` is omitted** from the update so Firestore keeps the existing pin; if the **location changed**, a new pin is required or save is blocked with a notify.
- **UI**: Event cards — **Pin set** (+ 5-decimal lat/lng) vs **No map pin** warning. Dialogs — status chips, **Use my location** (`getUserLocation`), collapsible **manual** lat/lng.

### 2. [`GooglePlacesAutocomplete.vue`](lil-magnet-memories/src/components/GooglePlacesAutocomplete.vue)
- Script loader uses **`VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY_TEST`**, then **`VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`**.
- Default **`types`** → **`['establishment', 'geocode']`** (only this component uses it today).

- Describes **new Places / `gmp-place-autocomplete`**, Market Events pin rules, **test key**, and **GCP** (Maps JS + Places (New), billing, referrers, migration links).

## Assistant

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed:

### 1. **“Missing: Location” after picking an address**
`gmp-place-autocomplete` often doesn’t push the chosen text into `newEvent.location` via `v-model` alone (nested ref + timing).

**Fixes:**
- In **`onCreatePlaceSelected` / `onEditPlaceSelected`**, set the address explicitly:  
  `newEvent.value = { ...newEvent.value, location: addr }` (and the same pattern for `editingEvent`).
- **`GooglePlacesAutocomplete`**: emit `update:modelValue` inside **`nextTick()`** (twice) so the parent updates reliably.
- **`createEvent` / `updateEvent`**: treat location as **`String(...).trim()`** so validation matches what you save.

### 2. **Show lat/lng as soon as they’re known**
Under the status chips, a **grey box** shows:

**Coordinates:** `lat, lng` **(selected place (Google) / manual entry / your device (GPS))**

If Google returns an address but **no geometry**, an **orange chip** and caption explain that and tell them to use GPS or manual entry (`place_no_coords`).

### 3. **Choosing an address overwrites GPS / manual**
On **`place-selected`** we now always **`createManualLat/Lng` (and edit) = ''** and set coords from the place when present.  
**Resolve order on save:** **place** → **manual** → **GPS**, so a new place pick wins over earlier GPS/manual.

### 4. **GPS**
**Use my location** clears manual fields so GPS isn’t blocked by old manual values.

## Assistant

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
1. **`element.setAttribute('types', …)`** – The new **`gmp-place-autocomplete`** widget doesn’t support the old `types` attribute. That triggered **`This property is not available in this version of the API`** and broke setup.
2. **`gmp-placeselect` + `event.detail.place`** – Current docs use **`gmp-select`** with **`event.placePrediction.toPlace()`**. The old event/shape often doesn’t run or doesn’t give a usable `Place`.
3. **Input not found** – The real `<input>` lives in the **shadow root**, often **after** a short delay, so one-shot `querySelector` could log **`Input element found: false`** and skip listeners.

### Fix (in `GooglePlacesAutocomplete.vue`)
- Stopped setting the legacy **`types`** attribute.
- When `props.types` does **not** include legacy **`geocode`**, set **`element.includedPrimaryTypes`** (up to 5). For Market Events, **`['establishment','geocode']`** still means **no** `includedPrimaryTypes` (same “venues + addresses” idea as before).
- Listen for **`gmp-select`** and **`gmp-placeselect`**, resolving the **`Place`** via **`placePrediction.toPlace()`** or fallbacks.
- **`waitForInnerInput`** + **`findInnerInput`** (shadow DOM) so the internal input is wired reliably.
- **`coordsFromLocation`** supports both **`LatLng`** (`.lat()`) and plain **`{ lat, lng }`**.
- Teardown on **`onUnmounted`** (listeners + poller). Short cooldown so both events don’t double-fire.

Docs updated in **`docs/GOOGLE_PLACES_AUTOCOMPLETE.md`**.

`npm run build` completes successfully.

### Diff (relevant files)

```diff
# See full patch with:
git diff -- src/components/GooglePlacesAutocomplete.vue docs/GOOGLE_PLACES_AUTOCOMPLETE.md
```

After deploy, you should see **no** `set types` error, **`Input element found: true`** (once the shadow input mounts), and **`place-selected`** with coordinates so **Create Event** can pass pin validation. If anything still fails, check the browser console for **`place-selected emitted, coords:`** and whether `coordinates` is non-null.

## Assistant

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### What the 500 means
The browser only sees **HTTP 500** from  
`POST .../api/send-status-update-email`. The real reason is on the **Cloud Function** (nodemailer/Gmail or a crash while building the email). Common cases:

1. **Email not configured** – `functions.config().email.user` / `email.password` never set for **`lil-magnet-memories`** (or wrong project).
2. **Gmail auth** – app password revoked/expired (`EAUTH`).
3. **Runtime bug** – e.g. `quantities` shorter than `photos`, or a bad `status` type breaking `formatStatusDisplay`.

### Code changes

**`functions/src/index.ts`** (and compiled **`functions/lib/index.js`**)

- **`getEmailConfig()`** – Uses **`functions.config().email`** *or* env vars on the function:  
  `EMAIL_USER` / `EMAIL_PASSWORD` (or `GMAIL_USER` / `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD`), optional `EMAIL_SERVICE`. Clear error text if nothing is set.
- **Order + contact + status emails** – All use `getEmailConfig()` (no duplicated config logic).
- **Status email** – `safePhotos`, **`normalizeQuantitiesForPhotos`** so missing/shorter `quantities` don’t break the template; **`escapeHtmlAttr`** on image `src` / `alt` and names; **`formatStatusDisplay`** safe for non-string `status`.

**`src/services/firebaseService.js`**

- **`sendStatusUpdateEmail`** – On non-OK response, reads the JSON body and logs **`error` / `details`** so the console shows the server message (e.g. “Email not configured…” or Gmail errors).
- **`updateOrderStatus`** / **`updateShippingStatus`** – Safer **`customer`** and defaults for **`photos` / `quantities`**.

### What you should do next

1. **Redeploy functions** (from repo root):  
   `firebase deploy --only functions`  
   (use the project that backs **`lil-magnet-memories`** / `us-central1`.)

2. **Confirm email credentials** for that project, either:
   - `firebase functions:config:get` and ensure `email.user` / `email.password` are set, **or**
   - In **Google Cloud Console** → your **`api`** function → **Variables**: set `EMAIL_USER` and `EMAIL_PASSWORD`.

3. **Retry a status change** and check the browser console; if it still fails you should now see the **exact `details`** string from the function in the error message.

4. **Optional:** In **Firebase → Functions → Logs** (or Cloud Logging), search around the time of the 500 for `Send Lil Magnet status update email error` for the full stack trace.

I didn’t run `git commit` / push; say if you want these changes committed and pushed to a branch.

## Assistant

Here are practical directions that match “paid, crawlable, and I can see users.”

## 1. Crawlable / metadata (SEO)

**Single-page apps (Vue/Quasar, etc.)** often need one of:

- **Prerender / dynamic rendering for bots**  
  Services like **[Prerender.io](https://prerender.io)** (and similar) render your app for crawlers and cache HTML. You pay for the service; your app can stay a SPA on normal hosting.

- **Host on a platform built for SSR/SSG**  
  If you’re willing to align your build with the platform:
  - **[Vercel](https://vercel.com)** – great if you use Nuxt/Next or can adopt SSR/ISR.
  - **[Netlify](https://netlify.com)** – prerender plugins, edge functions, good for hybrid setups.
  - **[Cloudflare Pages](https://pages.cloudflare.com)** + Workers for edge HTML if you want everything on Cloudflare.

- **“Real” SSR framework**  
  Nuxt (Vue) or Next (React) generates proper HTML per route with meta tags; then deploy to Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare. That’s the strongest long-term SEO story but is a product/architecture choice, not a drop-in.

None of these replace **good content, sitemap, Search Console, and correct meta**—they make it *possible* for Google to see HTML that matches what users see.

## 2. “See users on their site”

That phrase usually maps to one of these (often combined):

| Goal | Typical tools |
|------|----------------|
| **Who’s on the site right now / counts** | **Google Analytics 4** (Realtime), **Plausible**, **Fathom**, **Simple Analytics** |
| **Watch recordings of sessions (like being over their shoulder)** | **Hotjar**, **FullStory**, **LogRocket**, **Microsoft Clarity** (generous free tier) |
| **Errors + performance for real users** | **Sentry**, **LogRocket** |

These are **separate from** your SEO host: you add a snippet and pay the analytics/replay vendor. Many teams use **Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare for hosting + GA4 or Plausible + optional Clarity/Hotjar**.

## 3. One stack that often fits “pay + SEO + see users”

- **Hosting:** Netlify, Vercel, or Cloudflare Pages (pick what matches your build).
- **Crawlers:** Prerender.io (or platform prerender) if you stay SPA-only.
- **Visibility into users:** Plausible or GA4 for traffic; Clarity or Hotjar if you want session replay.

If you say whether you must stay on **pure client-side Vue/Quasar** or could move to **Nuxt**, and whether “see users” means **real-time counts** vs **session replay**, the shortlist narrows a lot. I’m in **Ask mode** so I can’t change your repo; if you want this wired into `lil-magnet-memories` specifically, switch to Agent mode and we can map it to your current deploy.

Use the Worker script from your repo: **`cloudflare/prerender.worker.js`**. Paste **everything below** into the Cloudflare Worker editor (replace the default code).

**Do not** put your token in the file. In the Worker → **Settings → Variables**, add a **secret** named **`PRERENDER_TOKEN`** with your Prerender token.

```javascript
/**
 * Cloudflare Worker: route crawler User-Agents to Prerender.io for Firebase Hosting SPAs.
 * Source: Prerender.io Firebase integration (maintained gist).
 * @see https://docs.prerender.io/docs/firebase
 */

const BOT_AGENTS = [
  'googlebot',
  'yahoo! slurp',
  'bingbot',
  'yandex',
  'baiduspider',
  'facebookexternalhit',
  'twitterbot',
  'rogerbot',
  'linkedinbot',
  'embedly',
  'quora link preview',
  'showyoubot',
  'outbrain',
  'pinterest/0.',
  'developers.google.com/+/web/snippet',
  'slackbot',
  'vkshare',
  'w3c_validator',
  'redditbot',
  'applebot',
  'whatsapp',
  'flipboard',
  'tumblr',
  'bitlybot',
  'skypeuripreview',
  'nuzzel',
  'discordbot',
  'google page speed',
  'qwantify',
  'pinterestbot',
  'bitrix link preview',
  'xing-contenttabreceiver',
  'chrome-lighthouse',
  'telegrambot',
  'integration-test',
  'google-inspectiontool',
];

const IGNORE_EXTENSIONS = [
  '.js',
  '.css',
  '.xml',
  '.less',
  '.png',
  '.jpg',
  '.jpeg',
  '.gif',
  '.pdf',
  '.doc',
  '.txt',
  '.ico',
  '.rss',
  '.zip',
  '.mp3',
  '.rar',
  '.exe',
  '.wmv',
  '.avi',
  '.ppt',
  '.mpg',
  '.mpeg',
  '.tif',
  '.wav',
  '.mov',
  '.psd',
  '.ai',
  '.xls',
  '.mp4',
  '.m4a',
  '.swf',
  '.dat',
  '.dmg',
  '.iso',
  '.flv',
  '.m4v',
  '.torrent',
  '.woff',
  '.ttf',
  '.svg',
  '.webmanifest',
];

export default {
  async fetch(request, env) {
    return await handleRequest(request, env).catch(
      (err) => new Response(err.stack, { status: 500 })
    );
  },
};

async function handleRequest(request, env) {
  const url = new URL(request.url);
  const userAgent = request.headers.get('User-Agent')?.toLowerCase() || '';
  const isPrerender = request.headers.get('X-Prerender');
  const pathName = url.pathname.toLowerCase();
  const extension = pathName
    .substring(pathName.lastIndexOf('.') || pathName.length)
    ?.toLowerCase();

  if (
    isPrerender ||
    !BOT_AGENTS.some((bot) => userAgent.includes(bot)) ||
    (extension.length && IGNORE_EXTENSIONS.includes(extension))
  ) {
    return fetch(request);
  }

  const token = env.PRERENDER_TOKEN;
  if (!token) {
    return new Response('PRERENDER_TOKEN is not set on the Worker', {
      status: 500,
    });
  }

  const newURL = `https://service.prerender.io/${request.url}`;
  const newHeaders = new Headers(request.headers);
  newHeaders.set('X-Prerender-Token', token);

  return fetch(
    new Request(newURL, {
      headers: newHeaders,
      redirect: 'manual',
    })
  );
```

That error means the Worker file has **`export default` more than once** (or the runtime thinks `.default` is declared twice). Cloudflare’s editor often starts with a small **Hello World** that already includes `export default { ... }`. If you **pasted the full Prerender script without deleting** that template, you end up with **two** default exports → **`Identifier '.default' has already been declared`** around the second one (~line 142).

### Fix

1. **Select all** in the Worker editor.
2. **Delete everything.**
3. **Paste the Prerender script a single time** — the version with **one** `export default {` block (the object that only has `async fetch(request, env)`).
4. **Save / deploy.**

You should see **exactly one** `export default {` in the whole file.

### Also check

- You didn’t **append** a second copy of the script after the first.
- You didn’t keep both the **starter** `export default { async fetch(...) { return new Response("Hello") } }` **and** the Prerender `export default`.

Summary of what was wrong and what we changed:

### Why Prerender still said “integration failed”

1. **Missing `www` route**  
   Your Worker only had `lilmagnetmemories.com/*`. A lot of checks (and users) use **`https://www.lilmagnetmemories.com`**, which never hit this Worker. In **Workers & Pages → `orange-feather-7607` → Settings → Domains & Routes**, add:

   - **`www.lilmagnetmemories.com/*`**  
   (same Worker as the apex route)

2. **Extension detection bug (fixed in repo)**  
   The Prerender gist used `pathName.lastIndexOf('.') || pathName.length`. In JavaScript, **`-1` is truthy**, so for paths **without** a `.`, it used `-1` and `substring` behaved badly. That could mis-classify paths vs static extensions. **`cloudflare/prerender.worker.js`** now uses:

   - `dot >= 0 ? pathName.slice(dot) : ''`

   **Copy the updated file from the repo into Cloudflare** (or replace that block), then **Save and deploy**.

3. **`.workers.dev` “nothing here yet”**  
   That URL is only the Worker’s **default** hostname. It is **not** your site and has **no** `lilmagnetmemories.com` route. Test with **`https://lilmagnetmemories.com`** (and **`https://www.…`** after you add the route).

4. **Token in a screenshot**  
   `PRERENDER_TOKEN` was visible as plaintext. **Rotate the token** in Prerender (**Security and access**), set it again in Cloudflare as a **secret** (encrypted), and avoid plaintext variables for production.

### What you should do now

1. Add route **`www.lilmagnetmemories.com/*`** → **`orange-feather-7607`**.  
2. Update Worker code from **`cloudflare/prerender.worker.js`** (extension fix).  
3. Rotate **Prerender token** and re-save it as an encrypted secret.  
4. In Prerender, run **Test integration** again.  
5. Optionally run:

   `curl -sI -A "Googlebot" "https://lilmagnetmemories.com/" | grep -i prerender`  

   You want a header like **`x-prerender-request-id`**.

`docs/PRERENDER_PATH_A.md` is updated with apex + `www`, verification notes, and the security reminder.

Here’s what a **Googlebot-style** request returns from here:

### `https://lilmagnetmemories.com/` (apex)
- **HTTP 307** → `Location: https://www.lilmagnetmemories.com/` (your canonical redirect to `www`).
- Prerender is in the path on that response:
  - **`x-processed-by-prerender: true`**
  - **`x-prerender-requestid: 52a32783-...`**
  - **`x-prerender-user-id: b305691d...`**
  - **`x-prerender-external-lb: haproxy-private-cache-6`**
- **`server: cloudflare`**, **`x-vercel-id`** → Cloudflare Worker → Prerender → Vercel, as intended.

### `https://www.lilmagnetmemories.com/` (after following redirects)
- **HTTP 200**
- Same style of Prerender headers:
  - **`x-processed-by-prerender: true`**
  - **`x-prerender-requestid: e8b194dc-...`**
- Body starts with real **rendered HTML**, e.g. **`<title>Home - Lil Magnet Memories</title>`** and your meta/CSS/JS links — not an empty shell.

So **Googlebot (and Prerender’s checks) are getting prerendered HTML**, with clear **`x-processed-by-prerender`** / **`x-prerender-requestid`** markers. That’s what you want for SEO and for Prerender’s dashboard.

*(The second `curl` used `-L` to follow the apex → `www` redirect; exit code 23 is normal when piping to `head`.)*

## Assistant

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed.

### Why reviews were empty
The app was only using **legacy** Place Details (`maps.googleapis.com/.../place/details/json`). Google often returns **`reviews: []`** there even when Maps shows reviews—policy/SKU limits, or the **Places API (New)** path being the one that actually serves review payloads for your project.

### What we implemented
`api/google-reviews.js` now:

1. Calls **Places API (New)** first:  
   `GET https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places/{placeId}`  
   with headers `X-Goog-Api-Key` and `X-Goog-FieldMask: displayName,rating,userRatingCount,reviews`.

2. Maps each new review into the **legacy shape** your UI already expects (`author_name`, `profile_photo_url`, `rating`, `text`, `time`, `relative_time_description`).

3. If there are still no reviews, it calls the **legacy** Place Details API (same behavior as before).

4. Resolves the server key as **`GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`** first, then **`VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`** (so you can use a server-only secret on Vercel if you want).

`env.example` documents optional `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`.

### What you should do next
1. **Deploy** this change to Vercel and ensure either `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` or `VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` is set for production.

2. In **Google Cloud**: enable **[Places API (New)](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/places.googleapis.com)**, keep billing on, and confirm your key is allowed for that API. Review text is tied to Google’s **billing SKUs**; if the New API responds with HTTP 403 or empty `reviews`, check the [Places API pricing / SKU](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/usage-and-billing) for your account (Enterprise / Atmosphere-style SKUs are often involved for full review content).

3. **Place ID**: Confirm `VITE_GOOGLE_PLACE_ID` matches the listing you linked (use Google’s [Place ID finder](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/examples/places-placeid-finder) on the business pin).

4. **Cache**: In the browser, remove `localStorage` key `google_reviews_cache` (or use devtools → Application) so you don’t keep an hour of empty results.

If, after deploy, the function logs show Places (New) succeeding but `reviews` is still empty, the next step is GCP billing/SKU or Google’s **Business Profile API** as the business owner—not more frontend changes.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
On Vercel, installs sometimes run **without devDependencies** (for example if the project is set to install production dependencies only, or tooling behaves that way). In that case:

- **`@quasar/app-vite`** was missing → `quasar build` failed (`quasar: command not found` or no `build` command).
- Even after fixing that, **ESLint** and the **TypeScript ESLint** stack were still dev-only → the Quasar ESLint plugin crashed loading `.eslintrc.js` (`MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `@typescript-eslint/parser`).

Locally you always had full `devDependencies`, so **`npm run build` passed** and hid the CI issue.

### Fix (pushed to `test-environment`, commit `820db22`)
1. **Moved into `dependencies`:** `@quasar/app-vite`, `eslint`, `eslint-plugin-vue`, `eslint-config-prettier`, `@typescript-eslint/*`, `typescript`, `prettier`, `autoprefixer` — everything required for `quasar build` + ESLint during the build.
2. **`vercel.json`:** `installCommand` set to **`npm ci`** so installs match `package-lock.json`.

Verified locally with **`npm ci --omit=dev && npm run build`** (production-style install) — build succeeds.

### Going forward
I’ll run **`npm run build`** (and **`npm ci`** when `package.json` / lockfile change) before pushing deploy branches unless you say otherwise.

If this Vercel project has **“Install only production dependencies”** (or similar) turned on, you can leave it on now; the build toolchain is in `dependencies`.

If the next deploy still fails, paste the Vercel build log snippet around the error and we can narrow it further.

Your screenshot from the Place ID Finder shows:

**`ChIJcw6BlkQL9YgRi2XERn80DPg`** → segment is **`Blk`** (capital **B**, lowercase **L**, **k**).

Your browser logs show the app using:

So the API was querying a **different place** (or an invalid id). Google still returned HTTP 200 with a **`name`** that looks right and **`reviews: []`**, which matches what you saw.

## Assistant

Here’s the distinction:

### On Google Maps / Search  
Reviews on your **Google Business Profile** are **public** in the normal sense: anyone who opens your listing can see them. There isn’t a standard “make my Google reviews private” switch for normal customer reviews like there is for, say, a private social post.

### Why that usually **doesn’t** explain your issue  
If reviews show on **Maps** for your business, they’re already **public on the listing**. The Places API doesn’t hide them because they’re “non-public” in that way.

What *does* match what you’ve seen is **API / billing / product limits**: the API often **omits** `reviews` / `rating` entirely until the right **Places** usage and SKUs apply—not a privacy toggle on the reviews themselves.

### Edge cases (uncommon)  
- Review **removed** or **still in moderation** → might disappear from Maps too, or be inconsistent.  
- **Fake/spam** handling → similar.  
- **Places API** still only returns **up to a few** reviews (often **5**) even when everything works—it never dumps “all reviews” like the full Maps UI.

**Bottom line:** Your reviews are almost certainly **public on Maps** if you can see them there. The empty API responses you’ve been debugging are **not** because Google marked those reviews as non-public; they point to **API access / billing / SKU** (or project/key mismatch), which you’re already chasing.

Here’s how that page fits what you’re doing, with the important billing detail.

### Place Details (New)

Official doc: [Place Details (New) – Web Service](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-details)

- Request: **`GET`** `https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places/PLACE_ID`
- You must send a **`X-Goog-FieldMask`** (no default fields).
- Auth: **`X-Goog-Api-Key`** (or key as a query param in some examples).

### Which fields cost which SKU (from that page)

Google groups fields by **SKU**. The doc lists things like:

| Tier | Example fields |
|------|----------------|
| **Essentials** | Address, location, `types`, etc. |
| **Pro** | `displayName`, `businessStatus`, icons, … |
| **Enterprise** | **`rating`**, **`userRatingCount`**, hours, phone, `websiteUri`, … |
| **Enterprise + Atmosphere** | **`reviews`**, **`reviewSummary`**, plus many “atmosphere” flags (`paymentOptions`, `editorialSummary`, …) |

So:

- **`reviews`** is billed as **Place Details (New) – Enterprise + Atmosphere**, not “basic” Place Details.
- **`rating`** / **`userRatingCount`** are **Enterprise** (separate from the `reviews` array).

That matches what you’ve seen: responses with address/name/types but **no** `rating` / `reviews` until the account is actually consuming those SKUs (and the key/project/billing line up).

### Legacy Place Details

The same doc set still points at [Place Details (Legacy)](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/details) for `maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/place/details/json`. Behavior is similar in spirit: review/rating data is tied to Maps Platform **pricing SKUs**, not “reviews are private.”

### Practical takeaway

Your integration should request e.g. `reviews,rating,userRatingCount` in **`X-Goog-FieldMask`** (which your server already does for the New API). If those keys stay missing in the JSON, it’s **billing/SKU entitlement** for **Enterprise** and **Enterprise + Atmosphere**, not a “public vs private review” setting on the listing.

If you want, we can align `api/google-reviews.js` field masks line-by-line with [the FieldMask section](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-details#fieldmask) so you’re explicitly requesting the minimum set for ratings + reviews.

Here’s what was implemented and what still depends on Google Cloud.

### Code changes (pushed to `test-environment`, commit `f83b0ff`)

1. **`api/google-reviews.js`**
   - Calls **Places API (New)** and **legacy Place Details** **in parallel** (faster, more chances to get data).
   - **New API** field mask includes: `displayName`, `rating`, `userRatingCount`, `reviews`, **`reviewSummary`**, **`googleMapsUri`** (aligned with [Place Details field groups](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-details#fieldmask): Enterprise + Enterprise + Atmosphere).
   - **Legacy** request uses atmosphere fields plus **`reviews_sort=newest`** and **`language=en`** ([legacy docs](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/details)).
   - **Merges** review lists from both APIs and **dedupes** by time + author + text prefix.

2. **`googlePlacesService.js`**
   - If there are **no individual reviews** but **`reviewSummary`** is present (AI summary), it builds **one card** so something can still show when Google withholds per-review rows but returns a summary.
   - Passes through **`reviewsUri`** / **`googleMapsUri`** for a “See all reviews on Google” link.

3. **`LandingPage.vue`**
   - Chip text **“Google summary”** when it’s the summary card.
   - **“See all reviews on Google”** button when `reviewsUri` is set.

4. **`scripts/check-place-reviews.mjs`** + **`npm run check:place-reviews`**  
   - Same parameters as production for local debugging.

### What code **cannot** fix

Google only returns **`reviews`**, **`rating`**, **`user_ratings_total`**, **`reviewSummary`**, etc. when your project is allowed to use the right **billing SKUs** (legacy **Atmosphere**; New **Enterprise** + **Enterprise + Atmosphere**). If those fields stay empty in the API, the UI will stay empty until billing/SKUs are correct.

### What you should do

1. Deploy / wait for Vercel build on `test-environment`.
2. Clear **`google_reviews_cache`** in the browser (or wait 1 hour).
3. Run **`npm run check:place-reviews`** locally — when you see non-zero **`reviewCount`** or **`hasReviewSummary: true`**, the site can show the same.

If you want, we can add a **Maps Embed** “Reviews on Google” block next (needs **Maps Embed API** on the key).

how do I get builling skus correct?

## Assistant

You don’t pick SKUs in a checkbox. **SKUs are chosen automatically** from what your API calls request and whether **billing is active** on the project that owns your API key. Here’s how to get that path “correct.”

### 1. One project, one key, one billing account

- In [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), open the **same project** where you created the **`places_api`** key.
- Go to **Billing** → confirm this project is **linked to a billing account** (not “free tier only” with no card).
- If you use multiple projects, the key in **Vercel / `.env`** must be from the project that has billing.

### 2. Enable the APIs (you’ve largely done this)

- **APIs & Services → Library** → enable:
  - **Places API** (legacy – used by `maps.googleapis.com/.../place/details`)
  - **Places API (New)** – used by `places.googleapis.com/v1/places/...`

Your key restriction list (Maps JavaScript + both Places) is fine.

### 3. Understand which **requests** hit which SKUs

From Google’s docs, **Place Details (New)** fields map to SKUs roughly like:

- **Basic / Essentials** – address, `displayName`, geometry, etc.
- **Enterprise** – includes **`rating`**, **`userRatingCount`**, hours, phone, `websiteUri`, etc.
- **Enterprise + Atmosphere** – includes **`reviews`**, **`reviewSummary`**, and many “atmosphere” flags.

Legacy **Place Details** splits into **Basic**, **Contact**, and **Atmosphere**; **`reviews`**, **`rating`**, **`user_ratings_total`** are **Atmosphere**.

So: **your app must be allowed to bill those product lines**, or Google **omits** those fields (what you saw).

Official overview:

- [Place Details (New) – FieldMask / SKUs](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-details#fieldmask)  
- [Legacy Place Details – fields / billing categories](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/details)  
- [Maps Platform pricing / SKU details](https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/sku-details)

### 4. Confirm in **Billing → Reports** (not only “$0”)

- **Billing → Reports** → filter **by project** (your Maps project).
- Add filters for **Service** = Maps / Places–related services.
- After you run `npm run check:place-reviews` or load the site a few times, you should see **usage rows** (and eventually non‑zero cost unless fully covered by credits).  
- If **Atmosphere** / **Enterprise** lines stay **empty**, either requests aren’t reaching Google with those fields, or billing isn’t attributing (wrong project/key).

### 5. Typical fixes when fields stay missing

| Issue | What to do |
|--------|------------|
| Wrong project | Recreate or copy the API key from the **billed** project; update Vercel env. |
| Billing not linked | **Billing → Account management** → link account; remove project budget blocks if you set a $0 cap. |
| Free trial / credits only | Still need a valid billing account; credits can cover cost but **SKU must still be billable**. |
| Key from different org | Use the key from the GCP project tied to **Maps Platform** billing. |

### 6. If it still doesn’t work

- **Google Maps Platform support** (same Cloud project): they can confirm which **SKU** each request hits.  
- As **Business Profile owner**, **Business Profile API** is a separate product for listing/managing the business; it’s not a substitute for fixing Places billing, but it’s another path for some owner workflows.

**Bottom line:** SKUs are “correct” when **billing is on the right project**, **Places APIs are enabled**, and your calls **request review/rating fields** (your server already does). After that, **Billing → Reports** should show usage on the **Atmosphere / Enterprise**-class SKUs; if it never does, the problem is still project, billing, or key mismatch—not the field list in your code.

## Assistant

In your situation there are **two different “enterprise” ideas** — only one applies to Places reviews.

### 1. **“Enterprise” on Places API (what the docs mean)**

In the Places docs, **“Place Details Enterprise”** and **“Enterprise + Atmosphere”** are **billing SKUs** (price categories), **not** a separate product you turn on called “Enterprise.”

You **do not** add “Enterprise” as a plan in the console the way you enable an API.

What happens instead:

- You link **billing** to the project (you already show projects linked to **Firebase Payment** billing accounts — that’s fine).
- You enable **Places API** / **Places API (New)**.
- When your app requests fields like **`reviews`**, **`rating`**, **`reviewSummary`**, Google **charges** (or counts) the matching **Enterprise / Atmosphere** SKUs **automatically** if the request is allowed.

So: **no extra “add Enterprise” step** for Maps SKUs — it’s **usage + field types + billing on that project**.

### 2. **If you mean “Google Cloud Enterprise” (support / contracts)**

That’s **organizational** (support level, agreements, discounts). You get that through **Google Cloud sales / support plans**, not via a single “Enterprise” toggle for Maps reviews. It’s **optional** and **not required** for the Places APIs to return review data.

### What to do practically

1. **Use one API key from the same project you’re billing** (e.g. `lil-magnet-memories-test` if that’s where the key lives).
2. **Billing → Reports** → filter by that **project** → after real traffic, you should see usage (and line items) for **Places** / **Maps**-related SKUs, including atmosphere/enterprise-class lines when those fields are actually returned.
3. If usage **never** appears for those SKUs but fields are still missing, use **Maps Platform support** on that project to confirm **which SKU** each request hits — that’s the right channel, not “adding Enterprise” in Billing → Projects.

**Short answer:** You don’t “add Enterprise” for Maps the way you add a subscription. **Billing + correct project + Places APIs + requests that include review/rating fields** is the path; “Enterprise” in the docs is the **name of the charge category**, not a separate enrollment step.

- **`/at-market`** → redirects to **`/?atMarket=1`** (same layout as home).

- **`?atMarket=1`** or **`?atMarket=true`** (case-insensitive) triggers **`setCustomerType('market_customer')`** only when **`marketEventService.getCheckedInEvent()`** is set (admin checked in, not checked out).
- **`marketDeepLinkApplied`** is set on success so geo logic does not override you.
- **`tryApplyMarketDeepLink()`** runs on mount, on **market event** listener updates, and when **`atMarket`** in the query changes.
- **`router.replace({ path: '/', query: {} })`** runs after a successful apply, or after the “no event” path (see below).
- **6s fallback**: if the query is still present, there’s still no checked-in event, and we haven’t applied the link → notify *“No live market event right now.”* and strip the query.
- **`calculateEventDistance`** returns immediately when **`marketDeepLinkApplied`** is true so location errors don’t call **`setCustomerType('online_customer')`**.
- Unmount clears the fallback timer.

### Links to use
- `https://<your-domain>/at-market`
- `https://<your-domain>/?atMarket=1`

## Assistant

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

**Cause:** The location field is a Google **`gmp-place-autocomplete`** web component. Updating `v-model` from the parent only changed Vue state; the visible text lives on the **host’s `value`** and/or the **shadow `<input>`**. The old `updateAutocompleteValue` often ran **before** the inner input existed, only did `inner.value = …`, and didn’t use the documented **`PlaceAutocompleteElement.value`** API, so the UI could stay blank even though `newEvent.location` was set.

**Fix (in [`GooglePlacesAutocomplete.vue`](lil-magnet-memories/src/components/GooglePlacesAutocomplete.vue)):**  
Replaced that with `syncModelValueToDom`, which:

1. Waits for `nextTick()`.
2. Sets **`host.value`** on the autocomplete element (per Google’s API).
3. Uses **`host.input`** when present, otherwise **`findInnerInput` / `waitForInnerInput`** so the shadow input is ready.
4. Updates the input, dispatches **`input`** / **`change`**, and runs **`validateInput`** so the field shows as valid.

The **`watch` on `modelValue`** is now `async` and awaits this sync whenever the parent sets the string (e.g. after “Use my location” + reverse geocode).

You should see the resolved address in the box immediately and be able to edit it before **Create Event**. No change was required in `MarketEventsPage` for this—the parent was already setting `newEvent.location`; the autocomplete needed to reflect it.

Prerender does **not** use a fixed “service” email you add in Search Console.

From [Prerender’s docs](https://docs.prerender.io/docs/integrating-google-search-console-with-prerender), you click **Connect Search Console** in the Prerender dashboard and then pick **the same Google account you use for Google Search Console** for that site. That’s a normal **Google OAuth** flow: **you** grant Prerender access to read your GSC data (e.g. sitemaps). There is no separate “Prerender email” to look up or invite.

If you see **“Insufficient permission”**, it usually means the Google account you used when connecting is **not allowed to manage that property** in Search Console (e.g. not an **Owner**, or you picked the wrong Google account in the OAuth popup).

**What to do:**

1. In Prerender, disconnect and reconnect, and in the Google account chooser pick the **exact** account that owns `www.lilmagnetmemories.com` in Search Console.
2. In Search Console → **Settings** → **Users and permissions**, confirm that account is at least **Full** (often you need **Owner** for third‑party linking to work reliably).

So: **no Prerender email to add** — fix it by using the **correct, high‑permission** Google account when Prerender asks you to sign in.

Those Prerender fields are just **your account profile**. The Search Console connection uses a **separate Google sign‑in (OAuth)** when you click **Connect Search Console**. Here’s what **Google (and Prerender, which renders your SPA)** can read from the **`<head>`** once the app has run.

### On every page that uses `MainLayout` (almost the whole site)

From [`MainLayout.vue`](lil-magnet-memories/src/layouts/MainLayout.vue), **one JSON-LD block** with:

- **`LocalBusiness`**: name, URL, logo image, short description, postal address (Dunwoody, GA), `sameAs` (Instagram).
- **`WebSite`**: site URL, name, `publisher` → that same business.

That is **in addition** to whatever each page sets below.

---

### Pages using `useSiteSeo` (same machine-readable bundle per URL)

For each of these, Google typically sees:

- **`<title>`** (document title)
- **`<meta name="description">`** and **`<meta name="keywords">`**
- **`<link rel="canonical">`** → `https://www.lilmagnetmemories.com` + current path  
- **Open Graph**: `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:type`, `og:image`  
- **Twitter**: `twitter:card` (`summary_large_image`), `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`  
- **`og:image` / Twitter image**: site logo URL on `www`, unless the page passes something else  

Implemented in [`useSiteSeo.js`](lil-magnet-memories/src/composables/useSiteSeo.js).

| URL path | Page | Document title | Notes |
|----------|------|------------------|--------|
| `/` | Landing | `Home - Lil Magnet Memories` | **`socialTitle`** for OG/Twitter: `Lil Magnet Memories - Custom Photo Magnets` (title in SERPs vs share card can differ). |
| `/about` | About | `About Us - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy from page. |
| `/products/custom` | Custom products | `Custom Photo Magnets - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/products/designer` | Designer products | `Designer Magnets - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/products/specialty` | Specialty products | `Specialty Products - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/contact-us` | Contact | `Contact Us - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/faq` | FAQ | `FAQ - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/event-calendar` | Event calendar | `Event Calendar - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/newsletter-signup` | Newsletter | `Newsletter Signup - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/shipping-info` | Shipping | `Shipping Information - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/returns` | Returns | `Returns & Refunds - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/leave-review` | Leave review | `Leave a Review - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/cart` | Cart | `Shopping Cart - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/checkout` | Checkout | `Checkout - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/thank-you` | Thank you | `Order Confirmation - Lil Magnet Memories` | Fixed copy. |
| `/photo-upload` | Photo upload | `Upload Photos - Lil Magnet Memories` | Same component as market variant. |
| `/photo-upload-market` | Photo upload (market) | Same as `/photo-upload` | Same `useSiteSeo` config; **canonical follows the real path** (so `/photo-upload-market` is distinct in `canonical` / `og:url`). |

---

### Product detail URLs (`/product/:productType/:productId`)

From [`ProductDetailPage.vue`](lil-magnet-memories/src/pages/ProductDetailPage.vue), Google gets **everything in `buildSiteSeoPayload`** plus **extra JSON-LD**:

**While loading or product missing**

- Title: `Product Details - Lil Magnet Memories`  
- Description: loading blurb vs “not available”  
- `og:type`: `website` (default)  
- Image: logo  

**When a product is loaded**

- **`<title>`**: `{product.description} | Lil Magnet Memories` (from your product field used as the title on the page).  
- **Description**: first ~160 chars of `detailedDescription` or `description`.  
- **Keywords**: includes product `category`.  
- **`og:type`**: `product`  
- **`og:image` / Twitter image**: first resolved product image (absolute `https://www...`), else logo.  
- **JSON-LD 1 – `Product`**: name, long description, image array, `sku`, `brand`, and **`Offer`** (USD price + `InStock` + URL) **only if** pricing yields a numeric price.  
- **JSON-LD 2 – `BreadcrumbList`**: Home → category hub (`/products/{type}`) → this product URL.  

Still gets the **sitewide `LocalBusiness` + `WebSite`** from `MainLayout`.

---

### Other routes (admin, diagnostics, legacy upload pages, 404, etc.)

They **do not** use `useSiteSeo`; many still set a basic **`useMeta`** (title/description only, no canonical/OG/Twitter bundle from the composable). They still receive the **MainLayout JSON-LD** if they render inside `MainLayout`. Examples: orders, admin, test runner, `ErrorNotFound`, etc.

---

### Outside the Vue app

- **[`index.html`](lil-magnet-memories/index.html)** has a default `<title>` / `<meta name="description">` from the Quasar template; after hydration, route-level meta **replaces** what matters for indexed URLs.  
- **[`public/robots.txt`](lil-magnet-memories/public/robots.txt)** / **[`public/sitemap.xml`](lil-magnet-memories/public/sitemap.xml)** are fetched as static files (sitemap lists public URLs including `/photo-upload-market`).

If you want this turned into a checklist against **live** Googlebot output, use the steps in [`docs/SEO_VERIFICATION.md`](lil-magnet-memories/docs/SEO_VERIFICATION.md).

## Assistant

What you see when someone searches for **your business name** (address, map pin, hours, etc.) almost always comes from **Google Business Profile** (Maps / local results), not from your website alone.

### 1. Change it in Google Business Profile (this is the main lever)

1. Sign in at [Google Business Profile](https://business.google.com/) (same Google account that owns the listing).
2. Open **Li'l Magnet Memories** → **Edit profile** / **Business information**.
3. **Address**
   - If you have a **storefront** customers visit, Google will usually **keep showing** a location; that’s normal for a “gift shop” style listing.
   - If you’re really **service‑area / no customer visits** at that address, you may be able to switch to a **service area business** and use Google’s options to **hide your street address** from the public (Google still keeps it for verification; what the public sees can change). Exact options depend on **business category** and how the profile was set up.
4. If the address is **wrong or duplicate**, fix or merge listings in GBP (and use [Google’s help for duplicate listings](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177)) so only one correct profile shows.

There is **no reliable “hide my address everywhere in Google”** for a typical retail / visitable location if Google treats it as the public-facing address of the business.

### 2. Your website (secondary)

Your site includes **LocalBusiness** JSON‑LD with a **postal address** (in `MainLayout.vue`). That helps Google understand the business; it does **not** replace GBP, and removing it from the site **won’t** remove the address from Maps/local pack if GBP still has it. It might only affect **rich result / snippet** use of address from your domain.

If the goal is “don’t publish address on *our* site,” you’d remove or narrow that schema (Ask mode: I can’t edit files here; use Agent mode if you want that changed in code).

### 3. What won’t work

- Editing **meta tags** or **Prerender** alone won’t strip the address from **Google Maps / Knowledge Panel** driven by GBP.
- “Deleting” the listing to hide the address also removes most of that discovery path—not usually what you want.

**Practical recommendation:** Decide *why* you want it hidden (privacy vs. wrong address vs. you moved). Then either **update GBP** (correct address, service area, or support case for duplicate/wrong listing) or accept that **verified storefronts** generally show an address in local results.

If you say whether you’re **storefront vs. service-only** and whether the shown address is **wrong or just too visible**, the exact GBP menu path is easier to narrow.

## Assistant

Here’s what that Search Console row is telling you and what to do next.

### What “Duplicate without user-selected canonical” means

Google thinks **this URL is a duplicate** of another URL (same or very similar content). For that URL, Google **did not** treat your declared canonical as the clear “user-selected” winner (or you didn’t give a strong enough signal), so it **did not index this duplicate** and may index the other version instead—or neither until things are clear.

So this is usually **one problematic URL pair**, not “the whole site is broken.”

### What to do (in order)

1. **Open the report and find the exact URL**  
   In **Indexing → Pages → Duplicate without user-selected canonical**, open the details and note **which URL(s)** Google lists as examples. That’s the only way to know if it’s e.g. `http` vs `https`, apex vs `www`, trailing slash, or a real duplicate path.

2. **Check that URL in URL Inspection**  
   - **URL Inspection** → paste the duplicate URL → **View crawled page** / **Page indexing**.  
   - See **“Google-selected canonical”** vs **“User-declared canonical”** (if shown).  
   That shows whether your `<link rel="canonical">` matches what you want (ideally `https://www.lilmagnetmemories.com/...`).

3. **Fix the cause (typical cases)**  
   - **www vs non-www / http vs https**: Only **one** should return `200`; the others should **301** to `https://www.lilmagnetmemories.com/...`.  
   - **Trailing slash**: Pick either always-with or always-without slash and redirect the other (if both `200`).  
   - **Same content on two paths** (e.g. old path still live): **301** the old URL to the canonical one, or add a clear **canonical** on the duplicate pointing to the preferred URL.  
   - **Query strings** (`?utm=`, `?ref=`) that serve the same page: canonical should usually point to the **clean** URL without params.

4. **Align with what you already ship**  
   Your app sets **canonical + `og:url`** via `useSiteSeo` on main routes. If the flagged URL is a route **without** that (or a non-`www` URL that still returns full HTML), that can cause this until redirects + canonicals line up.

5. **After fixing**  
   Use **Validate fix** on that report, and optionally **Request indexing** on the **canonical** URL in URL Inspection. Recheck after a few days.

### Important nuance

- **Not every URL needs to be indexed.** Duplicates are **supposed** to collapse to one canonical; the goal is **one clear winner**, not indexing every variant.  
- If the “duplicate” is e.g. `http://lilmagnetmemories.com/...` and you **301** everything to `https://www...`, that’s healthy; GSC may still show history until validated.

If you paste **the exact URL** GSC lists (or a screenshot of that example row), we can say precisely whether it’s a redirect issue, a slash issue, or a second path serving the same page.
