<user_query>
is there a way to automate the setup of the pages and the configuration on the business profile of different pages we have on the site?  Will that help get them indexed?  I want to be able to search for magnets, or gifts, or puzzle, etc, and get the site to come up.
</user_query>

## Assistant

Here’s a direct split between **what you can automate**, **what Google Business Profile (GBP) actually is**, and **what will help you show up for searches like magnets / gifts / puzzle**.

### 1. Automating “pages” on Google Business Profile

**GBP is not a copy of your website.**  
You get **one business profile** (per eligible location). You don’t create a separate GBP “page” for `/products/custom`, `/faq`, etc. So there is **no supported workflow** that means: “for every route on our SPA, create a matching GBP page.”

What GBP *does* have (varies by category):

- **Primary / additional categories**
- **Business description**
- **Services** (sometimes)
- **Products** (in some setups)
- **Posts** (short updates with links)
- **Photos**, **attributes**, **hours**, **service area**

**Automation:**

- **Google Business Profile API** exists but is aimed at **partners / multi-location / scale** use cases; many small businesses still use the **dashboard** only.
- Some **third-party tools** (Moz Local, BrightLocal, Semrush listings, etc.) help **sync NAP, categories, and sometimes posts** across directories — they don’t turn your whole site into GBP “pages.”
- **Your site** can be automated: build pipeline, **sitemap**, **meta per route** (you already use `useSiteSeo`), **structured data** — that’s the right place to automate “per URL” SEO.

So: **automate the website; treat GBP as one listing you enrich manually or with a listings tool, not as a mirror of every URL.**

---

### 2. Will automating GBP help **indexing**?

**Indexing** = Google **crawls and stores** URLs. That mainly needs:

- **Discoverable URLs** (internal links, **sitemap** in Search Console, not blocked by `robots`)
- **Stable canonicals** (you’re aligning on `https://www...`)
- **Unique, useful content** per URL

**GBP does not “index” your site’s pages.** It can:

- Show your **site link** on the knowledge panel
- Surface **Posts** or **products** that link **to** specific URLs (which can help discovery a bit)

So: **automating GBP won’t replace** good site structure + sitemap + content for indexing. It can **complement** local/brand discovery, not duplicate your whole IA.

---

### 3. Showing up for “magnets”, “gifts”, “puzzle”, etc.

Those are **very broad** queries. You’re competing with huge sites. Realistic goals:

| Query type | What usually works |
|------------|---------------------|
| **Local** (“photo magnets Dunwoody”, “custom magnets near me”) | Strong **GBP** (categories, description, service area, posts), **LocalBusiness** schema (you have it), **local** content. |
| **Product / intent** (“custom photo magnets”, “personalized magnet gifts”) | **Page titles**, **H1**, **body copy**, **FAQ**, **product names**, **internal links** to money pages. |
| **Single words** (“gifts”, “puzzle”) | Usually **not** realistic to “own” without a huge brand or very niche site; Google shows big retailers and entities. |

**What to do on the site (this is what moves the needle):**

- **Dedicated, keyword-aligned content** — e.g. landing sections or pages that naturally use “custom photo magnets”, “magnet gifts”, “photo puzzle” (if you sell puzzles) with **real** paragraphs, not keyword stuffing.
- **FAQ / blog** targeting long-tail questions (“best custom magnet gift”, “how to order photo magnets”).
- **Product titles and descriptions** in Firebase/CMS that include terms people search.
- **Internal linking** from home and category pages to those URLs.
- **Sitemap + Search Console** — already in motion; **request indexing** for important URLs after big content updates.

**GBP:**  
Use the **description**, **categories**, and **posts** to mention **gifts**, **custom magnets**, **events** — aligned with what you actually sell — so you help **brand + local** queries, not duplicate every site page.

---

### Bottom line

- **No**: There isn’t a standard way to **automatically create one GBP “page” per website route** or to fully sync GBP with every path like a CMS.
- **Yes**: You can **automate the site** (sitemap, meta, schema, content templates) — that’s what helps **indexing and relevance** for specific URLs.
- **Ranking for single generic words** is a **content + authority + time** game; GBP helps **local/branded** discovery more than winning “gifts” globally.

If you want a **concrete next step in the repo**, the highest leverage is usually: **one content pass** on [`LandingPage.vue`](lil-magnet-memories/src/pages/LandingPage.vue) + category pages + FAQ with natural phrases for “magnet gifts”, “custom magnets”, “puzzle” (if applicable), and ensuring those phrases appear in **titles** and **first paragraphs**. I can do that in Agent mode if you list the products/terms you care about most (e.g. puzzle vs only magnets).

## Assistant

You were right to call that out — I should have checked the Vercel logs before pushing.

### Why it failed
Vercel build error:
```text
Rollup failed to resolve import "pinia" from "src/stores/index.ts"
```

Locally, `pinia` was only available as a nested dependency of `@quasar/app-vite` (hoisted). A clean `npm ci` on Vercel (Node 24, no hoisting) could not resolve it, so the build failed even though `npm run build` worked on your machine.

The empty commit did not change app code; it exposed this existing gap on a fresh install.

### Fix (on `dev`, commit `014a27b`)
1. Added **`pinia`** as a direct dependency in `package.json`
2. Pinned **`engines.node`** to **`22.x`** (avoids Vercel auto-using Node 24 from `>=18`)
3. Added **`npm run verify:build`** → runs `npm ci && npm run build` (same steps as Vercel)

### Verified before push
- `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci && npm run build` — succeeded locally
- Pushed to `origin/dev`
- **Vercel: Deployment has completed** (success)

Preview: [Vercel deployment](https://vercel.com/mikeheldars-projects/lil-magnet-memories/9VyMpwjRDGXhUu7yHbXMS3eNgHxw)

### Going forward
Before any deploy push to `dev`/`main`, I will run:
```bash
npm run verify:build
```
and confirm Vercel/GitHub checks when possible.

`main` does not have this fix yet — only `dev`. Say if you want it merged to `main` as well.

## Assistant

You’re seeing a cascade from one root issue:

- `FirebaseError: auth/invalid-api-key` means Firebase Auth is initializing with an empty/invalid key.
- Then `[firebase-services] Firebase not ready, skipping` appears because the second plugin depends on Firebase init and bails out.
- Hydration mismatch happens because app init threw on client and the rendered tree diverged.

I fixed this on **`dev`** and redeployed:

1. `nuxt.config.ts`
   - Added env fallback so Nuxt reads both:
     - `NUXT_PUBLIC_*` **and** legacy `VITE_*` vars
2. `plugins/firebase.client.ts`
   - Added guard for required Firebase fields (`apiKey`, `authDomain`, `projectId`, `appId`)
   - If missing, it logs a clear warning and skips init (no startup crash)
   - Wrapped Firebase init in `try/catch` to prevent app-init fatal errors

Pushed commit: `9bea77f` to `dev`  
Vercel preview is now successful.

You can re-check on [dev.lilmagnetmemories.com](https://dev.lilmagnetmemories.com/). If you still see hydration warnings after hard refresh, send the exact route and I’ll do a second pass on that page’s SSR/client-only logic.

I added an automated scheduled Firebase Function that runs **daily at 9:00 AM (America/New_York)** and sends an **urgent reminder email to `lilmagnetmemories@gmail.com`** if there are open orders.

### What it does
- Schedule: `0 9 * * *` with timezone `America/New_York`
- Checks Firestore `orders` where `status` is one of:
  - `new`
  - `paid`
  - `in_progress`
- If none found: sends nothing
- If found: sends urgent email with:
  - order number
  - customer name
  - status
  - age in days
  - link to admin orders page
  - direct link to each Firestore order record

### Verification completed

```diff
 }
 
+function getOrderTimestampValue(order: any): number | null { ... }
+
+export const dailyOpenOrdersReminder = functions.pubsub
+  .schedule('0 9 * * *')
+  .timeZone('America/New_York')
+  .onRun(async () => {
+    const openStatuses = ['new', 'paid', 'in_progress'];
+    const snapshot = await admin.firestore().collection('orders')
+      .where('status', 'in', openStatuses)
+      .get();
+    if (snapshot.empty) return null;
+    // Build urgent HTML/text with links per open order...
+    await transporter.sendMail({
+      from: '"Lil Magnet Memories Alerts" <orders@lilmagnetmemories.com>',
+      replyTo: 'info@lilmagnetmemories.com',
+      to: 'lilmagnetmemories@gmail.com',
+      subject,
+      text,
+      html,
+    });
+    return null;
+  });
+
 // Export the Express app as a Firebase Function
 export const api = functions.https.onRequest(app);
```

- `C` (copying media into your own storage) mostly helps control/permanence and image performance, not core ranking by itself.

Implemented the full Instagram draft sync flow from the plan, including backend sync, idempotent upsert logic, auth/role protection, and Blog Manager UI wiring.

### What I changed

- Added new protected API endpoint `POST /blog/sync-instagram` in `functions/src/index.ts`
  - Verifies Firebase ID token from `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED_TOKEN]`
  - Allows only operator/admin emails (via `user_roles/roles_config`, plus initial admin allowlist)
  - Reads Meta credentials from env/runtime config:
    - `INSTAGRAM_USER_ID` (or fallback variants)
    - `META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (or fallback variants)
  - Pulls recent media from Meta Graph API
  - Maps each Instagram post to draft blog content
  - Idempotently upserts by `instagramSync.instagramPostId`
  - Tracks `createdCount`, `updatedCount`, `skippedCount`

- Added Instagram draft sync service method in `src/services/firebaseService.js`
  - `syncInstagramPostsAsBlogDrafts(limitCount = 20)`
  - Sends Firebase auth token to the backend endpoint
  - Returns backend summary payload and surfaces detailed errors

- Added Sync button and workflow in `src/pages/AdminBlogPage.vue`
  - New button: `Sync Instagram Posts`
  - Uses loading state `syncingInstagram`
  - Shows success toast with `created/updated/skipped`
  - Refreshes post table after sync

- `functions`: `npm run build` ✅

```diff
+  async syncInstagramPostsAsBlogDrafts(limitCount = 20) {
+    const currentUser = auth?.currentUser;
+    if (!currentUser || currentUser.isAnonymous) {

+    }

+    const response = await fetch(`${config.apiBaseUrl}/blog/sync-instagram`, {

+      headers: {

+        Authorization: `Bearer ${idToken}`,
+      },
+      body: JSON.stringify({ limit: Math.max(1, Math.min(50, Number(limitCount) || 20)) }),
+    });
+    // ...error handling + json return...
+  }
```

This isn’t a Blog Manager UI bug — **Instagram sync never runs** because the Cloud Function on `lil-magnet-memories-test` has no Meta credentials.

The console error says it directly:

> `Instagram sync is not configured. Set INSTAGRAM_USER_ID and META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN in function environment variables.`

The App Check warning is unrelated. Sync fails before it can fetch any photos.

### What you need

Two values from Meta, for the **Li'l Magnet Memories** Facebook Page with Instagram linked:

1. **Instagram Business Account ID** (`INSTAGRAM_USER_ID`)
2. **Page Access Token** with `instagram_basic` permission (`META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN`)

You can get these in [Meta Business Suite](https://business.facebook.com/) → your Page → linked Instagram account, or via the [Graph API Explorer](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/explorer/).

### Configure on test

Once you have those values, run (replace with your real values):

```bash
cd /Users/michaelhelman-darley/projects/lil-magnet-memories

npx firebase-tools functions:config:set \
  instagram.user_id="YOUR_IG_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID" \
  meta.page_access_token=[REDACTED]" \
  --project lil-magnet-memories-test

npx firebase-tools deploy --only functions:api --project lil-magnet-memories-test
```

Then click **Sync Instagram Posts** again in Blog Manager — photos should import into the draft grid.

I also updated the Blog Manager error toast so this “not configured” case shows a clearer message instead of a generic failure.

If you paste the Instagram Business Account ID and Page Access Token (or tell me they’re already in a local file), I can run the config + redeploy for you.

## Assistant

The handle you already use — **`@lilmagnetmemories`** / `https://www.instagram.com/lilmagnetmemories` — is not the same thing Blog Manager sync needs.

| What you have | Used for | Works for sync? |
|---|---|---|
| **Username** `@lilmagnetmemories` | Footer links, About page, SEO | No |
| **Instagram Business Account ID** (long number, e.g. `17841401234567890`) | Meta Graph API | Yes |

Linking to Instagram only needs the public URL. Pulling posts **with photos** through the API needs the numeric Business Account ID plus a Page access token.

---

### Easiest way: Meta Business Suite

1. Go to [business.facebook.com](https://business.facebook.com)
2. Open **Settings** (gear) → **Accounts** → **Instagram accounts**
3. Select **Li'l Magnet Memories** (or whatever the connected account is named)
4. Look for **Instagram account ID** — it’s a long numeric ID (not `@lilmagnetmemories`)

If you don’t see it there, use the Graph API method below.

---

### Via Graph API Explorer (if you have a Meta app / Page token)

1. Open [Graph API Explorer](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/explorer/)
2. Select your Meta app and generate a **Page access token** for the Facebook Page linked to Instagram
3. Run:

```text
GET /me/accounts?fields=id,name,instagram_business_account
```

4. In the response, find your Page and copy:

```json
"instagram_business_account": {
  "id": "17841401234567890"   ← this is INSTAGRAM_USER_ID
}
```

That number is what goes in Firebase config as `instagram.user_id`.

---

### Quick check from an existing post URL

If you already have a Meta Page access token, you can also run:

```text
GET /lilmagnetmemories?fields=id,username
```

That returns the Business Account ID for the username (only works with a valid token, not in a browser alone).

---

### What you still need besides the ID

Blog sync also needs **`META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN`** — the same Page token from Graph API Explorer or Business Suite. The username alone can’t authenticate the API.

Once you have both values:


## Assistant

Your footer/About links work fine on a personal account — those just use `@lilmagnetmemories`. **Sync Instagram Posts** in Blog Manager is different: it calls Meta’s official API, and Meta only allows that for **Business or Creator** accounts connected to a Facebook Page.

### Your options

**Option A — Switch to Business or Creator (recommended if you want one-click sync)**

This is free and your account stays mostly the same:

1. Instagram app → **Profile** → **Menu (☰)** → **Account type and tools**
2. Choose **Switch to professional account**
3. Pick **Business** or **Creator** (either works for the API)
4. Link it to your **Li'l Magnet Memories Facebook Page** (create one in Meta if needed)
5. Then get the numeric ID + Page token as described earlier

You keep posting the same way; you just unlock analytics and API access.

---

**Option B — Stay personal and skip the API**

You can still use Blog Manager without converting:

- **Paste photo URLs** into the featured image / photos section manually
- **Import Event Drafts** for market events (already works)
- Write posts by hand and link to `instagram.com/lilmagnetmemories/p/...`

There’s also a **Playwright scraper** in the repo (`scripts/sync-blog-seeds.mjs`) that reads the public profile without the Business API — but it’s a dev/build script, not wired to the **Sync Instagram Posts** button, and Instagram can block scraping over time.

---

**Option C — I wire up a non-API import path**

If you’d rather not convert the account, I could connect Blog Manager to the scraper approach (or a simpler “paste Instagram post URL → pull caption + image” flow). That’s less reliable than the official API but works on personal accounts.

---

**Bottom line:** Personal account + official API sync = not possible. Easiest path for automatic photo import is **Business/Creator + linked Facebook Page**. If you want to stay personal, say which you prefer — manual workflow or a scraper-based import — and we can set that up.

**Backend:** Firebase Cloud Functions (`functions/src/index.ts`)  
**Library:** [Nodemailer](https://nodemailer.com/)  
**SMTP:** Gmail with a **Google App Password** (not your normal Gmail password)  
**Single HTTPS function:** Express app exported as `api`

```2145:2146:functions/src/index.ts
// Export the Express app as a Firebase Function
export const api = functions.https.onRequest(app);
```

Frontend calls it at:

`https://us-central1-lil-magnet-memories.cloudfunctions.net/api`

(Test site still uses **production** for email/payments via `paymentsAndEmailApiBaseUrl`.)

---

## Credentials

Configured in Firebase (production project `lil-magnet-memories`):

```bash
firebase functions:config:set \
  email.user="lilmagnetmemories@gmail.com" \
  email.password=[REDACTED]" \
  email.service="gmail" \
  --project lil-magnet-memories
```

Code reads config in this order:

```23:46:functions/src/index.ts
function getEmailConfig(): { user: string; password: [REDACTED] service: string } {
  const cfg = functions.config().email || {};
  const user = String(
    process.env.EMAIL_USER ||
      process.env.GMAIL_USER ||
      cfg.user ||
      ''
  ).trim();
  const password = [REDACTED]
    process.env.EMAIL_PASSWORD ||
      process.env.GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD ||
      cfg.password ||
      ''
  ).trim();
  // ...
}
```

**Gmail setup:**
1. Enable 2FA on the Gmail account  
2. Google Account → Security → **App passwords** → create one for “Mail”  
3. Use the 16-character password **with no spaces** in config  
4. Redeploy: `firebase deploy --only functions:api --project lil-magnet-memories`

(`docs/GMAIL_AUTH_FIX.md` has the full troubleshooting steps.)

---

## API endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose | Sent to |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /send-order-email` | New order notification | Admin inbox (`emailConfig.user` = `lilmagnetmemories@gmail.com`) |
| `POST /send-status-update-email` | Order status change | Customer’s email |
| `POST /send-contact-email` | Contact form | Admin inbox, `replyTo` = customer |

Frontend calls (from `firebaseService.js` / `ContactUsPage.vue`):

- `config.paymentsAndEmailApiBaseUrl + '/send-order-email'`
- `config.paymentsAndEmailApiBaseUrl + '/send-status-update-email'`
- `config.paymentsAndEmailApiBaseUrl + '/send-contact-email'`

No auth token on these routes — they’re server-side only from your app.

---

## Important addressing rule (Cloudflare lesson)

Order & contact emails **do not** go to `info@lilmagnetmemories.com` directly. That domain forwards through Cloudflare and caused loops/suppression with Gmail SMTP.

Instead:

- **Authenticate as:** `lilmagnetmemories@gmail.com`  
- **Send `to`:** `lilmagnetmemories@gmail.com` (same account)  
- **`from` display:** `orders@lilmagnetmemories.com` or the Gmail address  
- **`replyTo`:** `info@lilmagnetmemories.com` (or the customer’s email on contact form)

```1643:1651:functions/src/index.ts
  const info = await transporter.sendMail({
    from: '"Lil Magnet Memories Orders" <orders@lilmagnetmemories.com>',
    replyTo: 'info@lilmagnetmemories.com',
    to: emailConfig.user,
    subject: subject,
    text: textContent,
    html: htmlContent,
  });
```

Status updates to customers use `from: emailConfig.user` and `to: customer email`.

---

## Scheduled email

`dailyOpenOrdersReminder` — Cloud Scheduler, **9:00 AM ET**, emails open orders (`new`, `paid`, `in_progress`):

- **To:** `lilmagnetmemories@gmail.com`  
- **CC:** amy + michael  
- Deployed with the same Gmail credentials

---

## What we’re *not* using

- **EmailJS** — still in `env.example`, but **not used** in the app anymore  
- **SendGrid / Mailgun** — not configured  
- **Vercel for email** — only used for things like Google Reviews / Instagram scrape

---

## Copy checklist for a new project

1. Add `nodemailer` to `functions/package.json`  
2. Add `getEmailConfig()` + `nodemailer.createTransport({ service: 'gmail', auth: { user, pass } })`  
3. Add Express routes (`/send-order-email`, etc.) on one `api` function  
4. Set `firebase functions:config:set email.user` / `email.password` / `email.service`  
5. Deploy: `firebase deploy --only functions:api`  
6. From frontend: `fetch('https://us-central1-PROJECT.cloudfunctions.net/api/send-...', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(...) })`  
7. Use a **Gmail App Password**, send to the Gmail inbox directly, set `replyTo` for branded replies  
8. Optional: scheduled function for daily reminders

If you want, I can scaffold the same minimal `functions/src/index.ts` email block for your other project.

## Assistant

Two issues were causing the Blog Manager Instagram sync to fail:

1. **500 on `/api/instagram-scrape-profile`** — Vercel was crashing when loading the scrape helper as ESM (`.mjs`). It’s now CommonJS like your working Google Reviews API.
2. **"body stream already read"** — On error, the client tried `response.json()` and then `response.text()`. It now reads the body once and parses it safely.

**Pushed to `test`:** commit `1b24970`

After Vercel finishes deploying (usually 1–2 minutes), try **Sync Instagram Posts** again on [test.lilmagnetmemories.com/admin/blog](https://test.lilmagnetmemories.com/admin/blog).

If it still fails, you should now get a clear error message instead of the stream error — paste that here and we can dig in. Instagram can still block some server IPs, but the Vercel deployment path should work since it’s the same pattern as Google Reviews.

## Assistant

The Vercel API is working now. The new error is different from before:

**Before:** Server crash (`FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED`)  
**Now:** Instagram is **rate-limiting** the bulk profile API (`429`) from Vercel’s datacenter IP

Single-post scraping still works — I confirmed that on test with a seed URL fallback.

**Pushed to `test`:** commit `85b9bf7`

### What changed
1. **Browser-like session** before calling Instagram (cookies + LSD token)
2. **429 retries** with backoff, trying both `www.instagram.com` and `i.instagram.com`
3. **Fallback:** when bulk profile sync is blocked, scrape individual post URLs instead (these work on Vercel)
4. **Clearer admin error** when rate limited

### What to do now

**Option A — Paste URLs (works immediately)**  
Use **Paste Instagram URL** in Blog Manager for each post. That path already works on test.

**Option B — Enable bulk sync fallback (recommended)**  
In Vercel → Project → Settings → Environment Variables, add:

```
INSTAGRAM_SYNC_SEED_URLS
```

Value: comma-separated recent post URLs from your profile, e.g.:

```
https://www.instagram.com/p/DZxtOyLvYr6/,https://www.instagram.com/p/OTHER123/
```

Copy 10–15 recent post links from [instagram.com/lilmagnetmemories](https://www.instagram.com/lilmagnetmemories/), redeploy, then **Sync Instagram Posts** will import those even when the profile API is rate limited.

**Option C — Retry later**  
Instagram’s limit is often temporary. Wait 15–30 minutes and try sync again.

---

After Vercel finishes deploying (~1–2 min), refresh Blog Manager and try sync again. If you haven’t set seed URLs yet and have no prior Instagram drafts, bulk sync may still fail with a clearer rate-limit message — that’s expected until you add seed URLs or import posts individually.

### Per-photo editor
- **Edit** button next to quantity on each preview card
- New [`PhotoMagnetEditor.vue`](src/components/PhotoMagnetEditor.vue):
  - **Mobile:** full-screen dialog
  - **Desktop:** inline expanded panel below the grid
- Pan/drag, wheel zoom, pinch-to-zoom, Reset, Fill square
- **Save** bakes a square JPEG (transform + frame) and updates the thumbnail

### Frames
- Global always-available frames from [`public/custom-border-frames/list.json`](public/custom-border-frames/list.json) (`alwaysAvailable`)
- Per-event frames: upload/remove in **Market Events → Edit Event → Upload Frames**
- Storage: `market-event-frames/{eventId}/...` via new `firebaseService` methods

### Upload/cart
- Submit paths upload `photoItem.file` (edited when saved)
- Cart photos include `editMeta` (frame + edited flag)

### New files
- `src/utils/photoItems.js`, `frameAssets.js`, `squarePhotoCanvas.js`
- `src/composables/useSquarePhotoEditor.js`
- `src/components/PhotoMagnetEditor.vue`

## Assistant

The Frame Management System is implemented across all five phases. Build passes.

### What was built

**Phase 1 — Frame Library (`/frame-library`)**
- New [`FrameLibraryPage.vue`](src/pages/FrameLibraryPage.vue): upload PNG, drag-reorder, delete, public toggle (admin only)
- Firestore `frames` collection + Storage at `frames/{frameId}/`
- CRUD in [`firebaseService.js`](src/services/firebaseService.js)
- Operator nav link + route with `requiresOperator`

**Phase 2 — Event frame assignment**
- [`MarketEventsPage.vue`](src/pages/MarketEventsPage.vue): multi-select picker from library (replaces per-event upload)
- Events store `selectedFrameIds` + `frameSortOrder`
- Auto-migration of legacy embedded `event.frames[]` into the library on first library load

**Phase 3 — Public catalog + featured schedules**
- [`frameCatalogService.js`](src/services/frameCatalogService.js): `resolveCustomerFrameOptions`, date-based featured ordering
- `frameCatalog/config` doc for featured schedules (admin UI on Frame Library page)
- [`PhotoMagnetEditor`](src/components/PhotoMagnetEditor.vue) + [`PhotoUploadPage`](src/pages/PhotoUploadPage.vue) use the new resolver

**Phase 4 — Frame Builder**
- [`FrameBuilder.vue`](src/components/FrameBuilder.vue): photo upload, stencil zoom/pan, adjustable center cutout, text + color layers
- [`bakeFrameOverlay`](src/utils/squarePhotoCanvas.js) exports transparent-center PNG + stores `builderRecipe` for re-edit

**Phase 5 — Print Template unification**
- [`PrintTemplatePage.vue`](src/pages/PrintTemplatePage.vue) loads frames from the catalog service
- Static [`list.json`](public/custom-border-frames/list.json) kept as fallback + auto-seeds library when empty

### Other changes
- Firestore rules for `frames` and `frameCatalog`
- Router: `requiresOperator` guard; Market Events now operator-accessible (not admin-only)
- Legacy `list.json` / embedded event frames still work until library is populated

### How to use
1. **Frame Library** → upload PNGs or **Create from photo**
2. Toggle **Public** for frames available on non-event uploads
3. Set **Featured schedules** for holiday pinning (admin)
4. **Market Events → Edit** → select which frames apply to that event
5. Customers at an event only see assigned frames; public users see public frames in featured order

Deploy Firestore rules before using in production. Say if you want this pushed to `test`.

## Assistant

Fixed and pushed to `test` (`877631c`). Here’s what changed:

### Save error
The `"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'path')"` error came from passing the Firebase **Storage Proxy** into `ref(storage, path)`. Frame uploads now use a real storage instance via `getStorage(getApp())`, same as product image uploads.

### Default 2 frames in library
Seeding no longer skips when the library already has other frames. On load it **upserts** `mitzvah_house` and `rythms_in_bloom` if they’re missing (fetches PNGs and uploads to Firebase when possible).

There’s also an **Import defaults** button on Frame Library if you need to trigger it manually.

### Frame Builder improvements
- **Text drag** — click and drag text on the preview to reposition it
- **Fonts** — Sans Serif, Serif, Script, Bold Display, Monospace, Comic, Elegant
- **Text size** — slider on the selected text layer (0.5×–3×)
- **Preview** — border photo shows clearly; center cutout is **grey tinted** (where the magnet photo will go); dark outer mask removed

After deploy, refresh Frame Library — you should see the two default frames. Try **Create from photo → Save** again; it should work now.

## Assistant

Fixed. When you opened a frame for edit, the image `load` handler was **resetting zoom/pan to defaults**, wiping the saved stencil transform — so the border looked thinner than when you saved.

**Changes:**
- On edit, the saved stencil (scale, x, y) is restored **after** the source photo loads, without resetting
- `viewportSize` is now saved in the recipe so pan position scales correctly if the editor viewport size differs
- Warns if the original source photo isn’t available (older frames saved before source upload was stored)

**Note:** Frames saved before this fix won’t have `viewportSize` in the recipe; re-save once after editing and it’ll stick. Frames missing the original source photo can’t fully restore — you’d need to re-upload the source.

## Assistant

Here's what changed in Frame Builder:

### Live font switching
The font dropdown was bound to a read-only computed property, so changes didn't always update the preview. It now updates the selected text layer directly, and the preview refreshes immediately when you pick a new font.

### Font preview in dropdown
Each font option in the dropdown renders in its own typeface — both in the list and in the selected value display.

### Overlay images (under cutout)
- **Drag & drop** images onto the preview square (highlight shows on drag-over)
- Or use the **Add image** file picker in the sidebar
- Overlays sit **below** the grey cutout box and **above** the background border photo
- **Click** an overlay to select it, then:
  - **Drag** to reposition
  - **Size** slider to resize
  - **Rotation** slider (0–360°)
  - **Remove** button to delete
- Text layers stay on top (above the cutout)

### Save / re-edit
Overlay layers are stored in `builderRecipe.overlayLayers` (position, scale, rotation, storage path) and baked into the final PNG. Re-opening a frame restores overlays for further editing.

## Assistant

Frame Builder now uses a unified layer system. Here's what changed:

### Unified layers
- **Images and text** are both layers in one list
- Drag an image onto the preview (or use **Add image**) → it becomes a new layer at the **top** (front)
- **Add text** creates a text layer the same way
- **Top of the list = front** on the canvas; drag layers in the list to reorder z-order

### Per-layer controls (when selected)
- **Move** — drag on the preview
- **Size** — slider (images: 5–85% width, text: 0.5–3×)
- **Rotation** — 0–360° slider (text and images)
- Text layers also get text, font (with live preview), and color controls

### Undo / redo
- Toolbar **Undo** / **Redo** buttons
- Keyboard: **Ctrl+Z** / **Cmd+Z** undo, **Ctrl+Shift+Z** or **Ctrl+Y** redo

## Assistant

Fixed and pushed to `test` (`dd201a2`).

**Root cause:** Global app CSS forces `Lato` with `!important` on all `span` and `.q-select` elements, so inline `fontFamily` on text layers and the font dropdown was being ignored.

**Fixes:**
- Text preview uses a CSS variable (`--frame-layer-font`) with `!important` so it wins over global styles
- Font dropdown options and selected value use the same pattern (including the teleported menu)
- Font binding uses `v-model` on a writable computed for reliable updates

Refresh and try changing fonts on a text layer — both the preview and dropdown should update correctly now.
